News.title: Eight in ten Brits rigidly follow same routine every morning – but just a third get up after first alarm
News.content:
SNOOZE CONTROL Eight in ten Brits rigidly follow same routine every morning – but just a third get up after first alarm

THE eternal morning routine debates have been put to bed once and for all – morning showers win, getting up after the first alarm without hitting snooze is best, and coffee beats tea.

A poll of 2,000 Brits revealed some very set opinions on the best way to start the day with 83 per cent rigidly sticking to a regime – although their approaches vary.



More than four in 10 (42 per cent) prefer to shower in the morning, while 23 per cent opt for a nighttime rinse – the rest have no preference or do both.

It also emerged 34 per cent get up immediately at their first alarm, while 26 per cent hit ‘snooze’ once or twice before rising.



And coffee is the preferred morning ‘fuel’ of choice (36 per cent) over tea (32 per cent).

For 25 per cent, adding milk before dropping in the tea bag is unacceptable – although nine per cent admit to doing this.



Almost half (47 per cent) check their phone within five minutes of waking up, with only three per cent resisting checking their device altogether.

One debate which remains unresolved however is whether to clean your teeth before or after breakfast.



Almost half (45 per cent) do so before and the same number (45 per cent) do so after, while 10 per cent have no particular stance.

Holiday Inn Express by IHG Hotels & Resorts commissioned the research and teamed up with comedian Rob Beckett, who launched The Great Wake-up Debate.

Discussing the campaign, which is inviting people to have their say on the right way to start the day, Rob Beckett said: “People will argue about absolutely anything, but morning routines are right up there with the best of them.

“You’ve got the annoyingly cheerful lot who are up, showered and chatting away before 7am — and then the rest of us, who need a bit of peace before we’re feeling properly human.

“What surprised me most is how seriously people take it — tea or coffee can divide a room faster than you can make either.”



The study also found 20 per cent will spend several minutes sitting on the edge of the bed ‘processing reality’ before finally getting up.

When it comes to the perfect condiment to go with their morning eggs, 18 per cent have eaten theirs with ketchup while ‘shockingly’ 13 per cent have tried them with salad cream.

As for baked beans, 32 per cent consider pairing them with mayonnaise to be “controversial”, while 33 per cent consider it similarly questionable to have them served on a croissant.

Other breakfast ‘crimes’ include pouring juice over cereal instead of milk (35 per cent).

While a quarter reckon milk should never go into the bowl before the cereal – although eight per cent are guilty of having done exactly this.



And although 15 per cent recoil at the thought of drinking the leftover cereal milk from the bowl, 26 per cent don’t share this stance and have happily downed it directly from the dish.

Almost two thirds (65 per cent) said their night-time habits directly affect how they feel the next morning with 49 per cent struggling to sleep unless they’re on their preferred side of the bed.

While peace and quiet (54 per cent), a cool room (51 per cent) and a duvet (35 per cent) topped the list of bedtime essentials.

Nearly half (45 per cent) sleep with just one pillow while 43 per cent favour a more elaborate three-pillow set-up.

Rob Beckett added: “For me, it all comes down to a good night’s sleep and a good brekkie to start the day.



“I’m a two-soft-pillows kind of guy and, while I’m usually up with the first alarm at home, I’m firmly “team lie-in” when I’m away.

“Even better when there’s free breakfast waiting, like at Holiday Inn Express – you’ll find me parked by the bacon and eggs!”

Generational quirks emerged too, with 21 per cent of Gen Z adults re-wearing clothes that aren’t entirely clean if they’re in a rush, compared with 16 per cent of Gen X and 14 per cent of Boomers.

And almost a third (32 per cent) of those polled, via OnePoll.com, said breakfast is the best part of a hotel stay.

While 20 per cent will book a hotel room without a second thought – if they know there is a comfy bed waiting.



John Wright, VP Mainstream Brands at IHG Hotels & Resorts, said: “The Great Wake Up Debate proves that everyone has their own morning habits and rituals.

“But what unites us is wanting to start the day feeling our best.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That’s why we focus on the essentials that matter most to our guests – comfortable beds with a choice of pillows, blackout curtains, bedside charging and our free hot breakfast.

“It’s all about making mornings feel a little easier and helping guests wake up refreshed, recharged and ready for whatever the day brings.”

News.title: Shocking moment ferocious leopard barges into booze shop and attacks terrified worker who scrambles behind counter
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a ferocious leopard barges into a booze shop and launches itself at a terrified worker.

Dramatic footage shows as the leopard leaps into the shop.



He immediately pounces at the shopkeeper in Todaraisingh, northern India.

The leopard uses its razor-sharp claws to swipe at Sanjay Gurjar, 25, and roars loudly.



The worker cries out in terror and the man and beast tussle.

Eventually Sanjay manages to push the animal away and scrambles behind the shop’s counter, before bolting out.

With his prey out of reach, the leopard slinks around the store.

It pushes boxes over and sends bottles crashing to the floor, then takes refuge under the counter.



Sanjay slammed the shop’s blind shut to trap the beast inside.

CCTV from outside the shop shows the leopard leaping at another man, Fateh Lal Koli, 40, before breaking into the booze shop and savaging the shopkeeper.

The clip shows Sanjay fighting off the big cat before leaping over the counter and fleeing.



Sanjay said: “I somehow pushed the leopard away and ran towards the exit.

“As I ran, I pulled the shutter down.

“Then I lost consciousness.”

The same leopard had attacked a third man that same morning, after wandering into town from nearby hills just before 9am.

It injured all three men and triggered a huge five-hour operation to track the predator.



Wildlife specialists finally tranquillised the leopard with a single dart at around 2pm, officials said.

The third man who was attacked by the beast was forest volunteer Rakesh.

He had been called out to check bushes where residents had spotted the animal, but was pounced on by the leopard.

The leopard then ran to the wine shop where it went for Fateh and Sanjay.

Sanjay suffered claw injuries to his hand, shoulder and nose and the two other men were also injured by the beast.



Police cleared 1,640ft cordon around the shop and shut the main market while they called in a specialist animal rescue unit.

The animal was a five-year-old male, officials said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He will be given medical checks before being returned to the wild.

News.title: Searches for holidays to Cape Verde up more than three times after African side’s World Cup heroics
News.content:
GREAT ES-CAPE Searches for holidays to Cape Verde up more than three times after African side’s World Cup heroics

SEARCHES for Cape Verde trips are up 265 per cent following the African country’s footballing heroics this summer, according to new data.

The small country which consists of 10 volcanic islands and has a total population of 491,233 stunned the world with their displays at the World Cup this summer.



The Blue Sharks were placed into Group H, alongside European big dogs Spain and two-time world champions Uruguay.

But against the odds, they held each of their group opponents to a draw to progress to the knockouts for the first time ever in the USA.



The footballing minnows then suffered a brutal 3-2 defeat to Argentina after extra-time in the round-of-32 after scoring two shock levellers.

And they impressed viewers so much, searches have increased dramatically compared to a year ago.

For anyone looking to experience it for themselves, the four-star Hotel Morabeza is recommended by the global marketplace.

Cape Verde forms part of Expedia’s 2026 Island Hot List, which highlights globally trending islands – with searches for island getaways up 55 per cent overall.

Each destination on the list falls into a different category, including the best romantic, wellness, nature, family, and affordable retreats – and more, with Cape Verde deemed the ‘best ultimate football-inspired island’.

Melanie Fish, travel expert and spokesperson, said: “The list was finalised until one destination generated so much buzz from football fans that we had to give them an award of their own.”



Other locations to make the list include St. Lucia ranking number one, which is considered to be the best for romantic escapes and Porto Santo, Madeira, Portugal, which is preferred for wellness and relaxation.

Praslin, Seychelles is best for nature lovers and Syros, Greece is top for cuisine.

Palawan, Philippines is perfect for natural wonders, and Culebra, Puerto Rico is best for water adventures.

Lofoten Islands in Norway also made the list, for its arctic adventures.

Meanwhile, Sanibel Island, Florida, USA is the location for family escapes, Phu Quoc, Vietnam is best for affordable luxury and Fiji comes top for ‘multi-generational value’.



Expedia’s Melanie Fish added: “Islands don’t just satisfy the urge to get away; they can also be one of the smartest holiday values.”

Travellers can unlock significant savings by bundling flights, hotels, car hire and activities on Expedia – booking everything together can save hundreds on average, while simplifying planning.

High-demand islands fill up fast, especially during peak holiday periods – booking early helps secure the best rates and availability.

News.title: Is there a deputy Prime Minister in Andy Burnham’s new Labour Cabinet?
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has walked into 10 Downing Street as Britain’s new Prime Minister, unveiling a revamped Labour Cabinet to deliver his 10-year plan for the country.

As the new Prime Minister reshuffles the frontbench, voters are looking closely at who is running the country alongside him.



While John Healey has taken over from Rachel Reeves as Chancellor and Ed Miliband steps into the Foreign Office, one major title appears to be missing – Deputy Prime Minister.

Is there a Deputy Prime Minister in Andy Burnham’s Cabinet?

Technically, no minister in Andy Burnham’s new Cabinet holds the official job title of “Deputy Prime Minister.”



The previous post-holder, David Lammy, was removed from office when Burnham took over from Sir Keir Starmer and cleared out key figures from the previous administration.

Former Deputy PM Angela Rayner has returned to Cabinet, but as Housing Secretary.



Instead of naming a formal Deputy Prime Minister, Burnham has appointed his long-time ally Louise Haigh as First Secretary of State.

In the British political system, First Secretary of State is the highest-ranking Cabinet post after the Prime Minister.

It outranks all other Secretaries of State and carries automatic seniority across Whitehall.

By pairing Haigh in this post with Lucy Powell‘s role as Deputy Leader of the Labour Party, Burnham has established a clear hierarchy at No10 without needing to hand out a separate “Deputy PM” badge.



Who is Louise Haigh?

Louise Haigh is the MP for Sheffield Heeley and one of Andy Burnham’s most powerful political allies.

Haigh previously served as Transport Secretary under Starmer before resigning in late 2024 after pleading guilty to fraud by misrepresentation over a work mobile phone incident.

After returning to the backbenches, she became a key architect behind Burnham’s political comeback, managing his campaign in the Makerfield by-election and orchestrating his bid for the Labour leadership.

Alongside her title as First Secretary of State, Haigh has been appointed Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster and Minister for the Cabinet Office.

The Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster is one of Britain’s oldest ministerial roles.



Because the position does not oversee a single spending department like Health or Defence, the minister operates as a “minister without portfolio.”

This leaves Haigh free to manage the Cabinet Office, coordinate cross-government strategy, and resolve disputes between departments.

Under Burnham, Haigh’s department has been beefed up to act as the “political engine room” driving Downing Street’s economic and social policies.

As First Secretary of State and Cabinet Office chief, Haigh holds senior Cabinet rank and controls the day-to-day machinery of government, making her Burnham’s de facto second-in-command.



Does Burnham have to appoint a Deputy PM?

Andy Burnham is under no constitutional or legal obligation to name an official Deputy Prime Minister.

Under Britain’s unwritten constitution, the title of Deputy Prime Minister is discretionary.

It is a title a Prime Minister can choose to grant or leave empty.

Past leaders, including Margaret Thatcher, Tony Blair for parts of his tenure, and Theresa May, governed the country without ever naming an official Deputy PM.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Burnham could give the “Deputy Prime Minister” title to Haigh or another Cabinet minister during a future reshuffle.



But because First Secretary of State already carries senior deputy status and allows the holder to stand in for the PM at PMQs or chair Cabinet meetings if required, Burnham may keep the current arrangement.

News.title: Evil blade trio jailed for 46 YEARS for brutal beach murder of Kayden Moy
News.content:
THREE teenage killers have been jailed for a total of 46 years for the horror beach murder of Kayden Moy.

Cole Turley, 18, Jay Stewart, 18 and a boy of 15 we can’t name for legal reasons knifed the 16-year-old to death on Irvine Beach, Ayrshire, as hundreds of youngsters enjoyed a heatwave in May 2025.



Turley admitted to the savage killing, while a jury found Stewart and the 15-year-old guilty of murder last month following a trial at the High Court in Glasgow.

The trio of thugs – all members of the Murray Boys group that terrorised East Kilbride, Lanarkshire – have now been locked up for the crime.



Jay Stewart, 19, Cole Turley, 18 and a 15-year-old were sentenced at Glasgow High Court to a minimum of 16, 16 and 14 years detention respectively.

Judge Lord Scott today/yesterday sentenced Turley to 16 years. Stewart was jailed for 16 years which will be initially served in a young offenders insititution.



The 15-year-old was given 14 years which will start in secure accommodation until he is 19.

The judge told the trio: “Your emphasis being intoxication through drunk or drugs is no excuse whatsoever.

“Three young people travelled to Irvine Beach armed with the intent on reprisal for some slight hurt caused to someone associated with your group. Two of you took weapons.

“In the case of Cole Turley, a knife was taken which was used to stab and murder.



“Kayden Moy’s death was pointless and unnecessary.

“The victim could have been anyone in the group. Kayden was the one who slipped and fell.

“You did not care whether he lived or died and celebrated what you did.

“Despite claims of intoxication, you had the presence of mind in the aftermath to conceal your involvement in the appalling crime consistent with this being a planned attack. The sentence for murder is a life sentence.”

After the sentencing was heard, members of family and friends in the public gallery became animated with each other with shouts of “scumbags” heard. A number of police officers in the court had to become involved to separate both sides.



Kayden’s heartbroken dad spoke outside court after the sentencing while being supported by friends and relatives.

He said: “”Today, the three boys responsible for taking our son Kayden’s life have finally been sentenced.

“While today’s outcome brings a measure of justice, it does not bring our son back.

“Kayden was more than a name in a courtroom or a headline in the news. He was our son.

“He was much loved beyond words and had his whole life ahead of him.



“Every birthday, every family gathering and every milestone from now on will be a reminder that he should be here with us.

“That is the life sentence which our family has been given.

“The choices made that day have had devastated our family forever.

“It is a clear message that violence has clear devastating consequences.

“One moment of violence has destroyed many lives.



“No family should have to endure the pain that we now live with every day.

“More importantly, we want people to remember Kayden not for how he died but for how he lived.

“He will always be our son, he will always be loved and missed.

“His name will never be forgotten and we will continue to speak about him for the rest of our lives.”

There were emotional scenes outside court as Kayden’s heartbroken family celebrated his killers being nailed.



In a message on social media posted ahead of the sentencing, Kayden’s father Paul Moy said: “Nothing that happens in that courtroom will ever bring our son back.

“No sentence can fill the emptiness, the heartbreak, or the lifetime of memories we’ve been robbed of.

“Tomorrow is not about closure, because there is no such thing when you lose a child.



“It is about justice, accountability, and making sure my son’s life is remembered.

“Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever my son.”

Sickening CCTV footage showed the teen killers celebrating the murder as they fled the scene.



In shameful scenes at the High Court in Glasgow, Stewart smirked at Kayden’s grieving loved ones as he was nailed for murdering the apprentice painter and decorator.

And a sick woman taunted the victim’s parents by shouting: “At least my son’s still alive.”

Serial blade thug Stewart had also dodged jail for having a machete just four days before the murder. The yob also had a previous conviction for a breach of the peace with a knife.

During the trial the jury heard that shortly before the attack Turley, Stewart, and the 15-year-old had been at the top of a sand dune throwing rocks at people on the beach.

Kayden’s girlfriend Keryn Knox, who had been with him at the beach, said they had been getting ready to leave at about 6pm when the rocks started to be thrown, and Kayden had gone up to confront the teenagers.



Ms Knox told the court: “I went up with him to try and stop him. At that point he had run up the hill and he was just shouting stuff back.

“Then Cole ran in from the side and Kayden has seen a blade and when he tried to run he slipped, and when he tried to get back up Cole has stabbed him in his left lower side twice.”

Ms Knox told the court: “His body turned completely white and his limbs were blue and people were crowding round him, trying to put his T-shirt over the wound.”



Another witness said he had gone with Kayden to confront the teenagers, and that as they reached the top of the dune, Turley brought out a knife and Stewart an extendable baton.

The witness said: “Then out of nowhere Cole (Turley) just started running at us. I ran to the right, so did Kayden, I jumped over a grass ledge, Kayden slipped and Cole leaped over and jumped on him.

“He had a knife and it hit. I saw one stab.”

The 16-year-old was so badly injured in the attack that he later died.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Stewart and the 15-year-old had denied the murder charge and had lodged special defences of incrimination.



However this was rejected by the jury, who found both guilty of Kayden’s murder after a trial lasting more than two weeks.

News.title: From fraudster Haigh to shock pick Healey…everything you need to know about Burnham’s Cabinet & what it means
News.content:
ANDY Burnham finalised his top team yesterday evening after executing a brutal purge of Sir Keir Starmer’s cabinet allies.

Now Mr Burnham will hold his first cabinet after officially becoming Prime Minister this afternoon.



But who are the new figures who will oversee the economy, the UK’s borders and energy policy – and where do they sit on the political spectrum?

John Healey – Chancellor



In a major surprise to Westminster onlookers, Mr Healey was appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer after Rachel Reeves was sacked.

The former defence secretary was scathing of Sir Keir Starmer after he failed to set a date of when defence spending would be boosted to 3 per cent of GDP.



He is seen as a moderate in the Labour Party and was a member of a group called Labour First – originally set up to take on the Hard Left.

Mr Healey was first elected as an MP in 1997 and served as a Treasury minister under Tony Blair between 2002-2007.

His appointment won plaudits across the political spectrum, including from Tory leader Kemi Badenoch and Lib Dem leader Ed Davey.



Louise Haigh – First Secretary of State

Ms Haigh has been appointed First Secretary of State, essentially taking on the role as COO of the UK.

She will act as Mr Burnham’s deputy, stepping in for when he’s away and helping different cabinet ministers work together when their roles overlap.

Sheffield-born Ms Haigh is a close friend and ally of Mr Burnham having helped plot his route back to Westminster for “at least the last year”.

Sir Keir Starmer sacked her as transport secretary after she admitted to being a convicted fraudster after telling cops her phone was stolen.



Ms Haigh was criticised in her role as transport secretary after handing striking train drivers billions in pay rises in the very week pensioners were robbed of their winter fuel payments.

Angela Rayner – Housing Secretary

After dramatically leaving Government last year, Ms Rayner finally has her old job back as Housing Secretary.

She left her role as cabinet minister after it was revealed she underpaid £40,000 on a flat in Hove.



Ms Rayner claimed she had been “exonerated” by HMRC after paying back the shortfall — and received no penalty.

While she was out of Government she made increasingly Left-wing noises, calling immigration reforms to indefinite leave to remain (ILR) as “un-British”.

Ms Rayner never had the numbers to launch a leadership bid of her own, so she ended up rowing in behind Mr Burnham.

Ed Miliband – Foreign Secretary



Net Zero zealot Ed Miliband has been moved from the Energy department to the Foreign Office.

He will pick up the reins as Foreign Secretary while the brutal war in Ukraine continues and the crisis in the Middle East unfolds.

Mr Miliband, who led the Labour Party between 2010-2015, was highly tipped to be appointed as Chancellor, as Left-wing Labour MPs lobbied him for the role.

He will now be globe trotting to act as a representative of the UK on the world stage.



Mr Miliband was seen as instrumental in getting Mr Burnham back into Parliament and told Sir Keir that the game was up early on.

Wes Streeting – Defence Secretary

Mr Streeting served as Sir Keir’s health secretary before spectacularly resigning after Labour’s disastrous set of local elections results in May.

He was seen as a relatively successful Health Secretary after bringing NHS waiting lists down and is one of the party’s better communicators.



The ex-cabinet minister stood down from Government after declaring he had no confidence in Sir Keir’s leadership.

He was seen as a potential front runner for the Labour leadership until Mr Burnham won his seat in Makerfield last month.

Mr Streeting rowed in behind him and has been rewarded as Defence Secretary.

Shabana Mahmood – Home Secretary

Ms Mahmood has seen an extraordinary rise from Justice Secretary in 2024 to Home Secretary in 2025.



She is a hardliner on migration having announced plans to double the amount of time it takes to qualify for indefinite leave to remain (ILR), which gives migrants the rights to claim benefits and live in the UK permanently.

Ms Mahmood is seen to be on the right of the party on social and cultural issues, but was also highly tipped for job of Chancellor.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She was one of the first ministers to privately call for Sir Keir to set out a timeline for his resignation.

ANALYSIS: So what does Andy's Cabinet mean? By Tom Scotson, Political Correspondent After celebrating with his northern supporters outside Downing Street, Andy Burnham had to crack on with the first difficult task of his premiership – upsetting MPs. The new Prime Minister had to finalise who would be in his top team and, most importantly, take the coveted job of Chancellor. Labour MPs and Westminster insiders were quietly surprised John Healey was picked for the top job in the Treasury. But across the party he is seen as a smart pick for several reasons. The Tories will find it harder to throw mud at him after praising Mr Healey for resigning as Defence Secretary last month, lambasting Sir Keir Starmer for failing to set a date for when the UK should spend three per cent of GDP on defence. He is also on the traditional Right of the party too, and will be more in touch with the public mood than someone like eco-zealot Ed Miliband, who is willing to destroy the economy in his pursuit of Net Zero. Instead Mr Miliband was plonked in as foreign secretary, now out of sight and out of mind for Mr Burnham. This could prove vital for the PM when things get rocky, as Mr Miliband still maintains huge respect on the Labour backbenchers. Fundamentally, the Cabinet is more mixed in terms of ideology than many thought. It includes embattled Left-wingers such as Louise Haigh, Angela Rayner and Lucy Powell. But Mr Burnham has made the eminently sensible decision to keep Shabana Mahmood as Home Secretary, who is continuing to crack down on legal and illegal migration.

News.title: Is Keir Starmer still an MP and what will the former Prime Minister do now he’s resigned?
News.content:
SIR KEIR STARMER has departed Downing Street, delivering his final speech as Prime Minister following his resignation.

After leading the government through two event-filled years, the political landscape in Westminster has been turned on its head.

As the Labour Party transitions to new leadership, voters and constituents across the country are asking what comes next for the outgoing leader.



Is Keir Starmer still an MP – where is his constituency?

When a Prime Minister resigns from their executive role in government or steps down as leader of their political party, they do not lose their seat in the House of Commons.



Sir Keir continues to serve as a backbench Member of Parliament.

His constituency is Holborn and St Pancras in North London.

Starmer has represented Holborn and St Pancras since May 2015, having defended the seat in subsequent general elections.

Unless he chooses to resign his parliamentary seat, he remains the elected representative for the area, handling constituent work and voting on legislation.

What could Keir Starmer do next?

Sir Keir faces a choice that every former leader encounters upon leaving top office.

He could remain in Parliament as an active backbencher, focusing on local casework or international foreign policy.

But he could choose to retire from Parliament altogether to pursue private sector roles, legal practice, or international diplomatic work.



Retiring as an MP would represent a major political gamble for the Labour Party.

If Starmer resigns as an MP, it would trigger an immediate by-election in Holborn and St Pancras.

Under the leadership of Zack Polanski, the Greens have gained significant ground across central London.

Polanski’s party has actively targeted Labour’s traditional urban strongholds, squeezing support in key capital constituencies.

Polanski has previously said it would be “tempting” to challenge Starmer for his parliamentary seat, hinting that he may run for Holborn and St Pancras if it were to become available.



A by-election in Holborn and St Pancras would force Labour to defend a high-profile seat against a big-name candidate.

Losing or suffering a heavy vote drop to Polanski’s Greens would deal a severe psychological blow to Labour’s momentum.

Because of this threat, party strategists may encourage Starmer to hold onto his seat to avoid triggering a risky London by-election.

What have other Prime Ministers done after leaving No10?

Former Prime Ministers have taken very different paths after leaving Downing Street.

Theresa May stayed on as the MP for Maidenhead for nearly five years after leaving No10, providing experience from the backbenches before retiring from Parliament in 2024.



Rishi Sunak retained his constituency seat in Richmond and Northallerton, choosing to stay in the House of Commons as a backbencher.

Boris Johnson briefly stayed on as MP for Uxbridge and South Ruislip before stepping down from Parliament to pursue journalism, writing, and international speaking engagements.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

David Cameron stayed on as MP in 2016 before quickly resigning his seat, later making a return to frontline politics as Foreign Secretary under Rishi Sunak.

Tony Blair stood down as MP upon leaving Downing Street in 2007 to take on high-profile international envoy and advisory roles.

News.title: Girl, 11, died in River Thames after asking dad if she could 'dip her toes'
News.content:
Girl, 11, died in River Thames after asking dad if she could 'dip her toes'

Kaliyah Coa disappeared after entering the River Thames at Barge House Causeway, east London, sparking a large-scale search before her body was found

View 2 Images Kaliyah Coa died after entering the River Thames (Image: Metropolitan Police / SWNS)

An 11-year-old girl died in the River Thames after asking her dad if she could "dip her toes" in the water, an inquest heard.

‌



Kaliyah Coa disappeared after entering the water at Barge House Causeway, east London, on March 31, 2025, sparking a large-scale search of the river before her body was found.

‌



At an inquest at the East London Coroner's Court on Thursday (July 16) attended by her parents, grandmother, uncle, and aunts, the death was recorded as accidental.

‌



Coroner Graeme Irvine concluded that Kaliyah died from immersion in the River Thames. He said: "It seems to me that the only short-form conclusion I can give is accidental death."

View 2 Images A major search was launched by Barge House Causeway for Kaliyah (Image: PA)

Iran-backed group declares another crucial strait closed as Middle East war widens READ MORE :

The court heard Kaliyah had attended a birthday party the day before her death, before asking her father if she could stay for a sleepover.

‌



In a statement read to the court, Mr Coa said he had initially been against the sleepover because it would have been the first time Kaliyah had stayed at the address.

However, after speaking with the other child's father, he agreed. He said: "I didn't want to spoil the fun, so I said it was okay."

The inquest heard the children made themselves breakfast the following morning before going to a nearby park. Later, they made their way to Barge House Causeway beside the River Thames.

‌



The court heard Kaliyah spoke to her father while she was near the river. Mr Coa said she told him she was near the Thames, adding he would have been "more relieved" if she had gone to a nearby park instead.

He said Kaliyah asked if she could "dip her toes" in the water. Mr Coa's statement said that he "reminded her that where she was, was not a beach."

He said he raised his voice and told his daughter to move away from the water, with Kaliyah replying: "Pops, I know about the currents." Mr Coa said he initially thought Kaliyah being near the river "was a joke" and he later added: "I was now angry that no adult from the house didn't tell me they were outside."

‌



The court heard Nathan Guy, who lived overlooking the jetty, called 999 after witnessing what happened. In a statement read to the court, Mr Guy said he saw five children playing near the jetty.

He heard one child say: "You made me throw it." The inquest heard one of the children had lost a shoe in the river and Kaliyah tried to help retrieve it.

Mr Guy said Kaliyah used a scooter to try to reach the shoe before another child told her: "It's too expensive, don't use that." He said to police: "I saw the girl by the river. I called 999 and went back to the door and saw the girl struggling in the water. I turned away then I saw her head under the water."

‌



Mr Guy said the weather was sunny and there was no obstruction to his view. Mr Irvine said there was no evidence of hostility between the children, describing what happened as "play", and he added there was no evidence of deliberate bullying or any "dark intent."

The coroner said: "These were children who were friends. It is a testament of Kaliyah as a confident and helpful and kind child that she tried to help her friend." After a search operation involving emergency services and the Coastguard, Kaliyah's body was recovered from the Thames on April 13, 2025.

Professor Alan Bates, the coroner's pathologist and forensic medical expert, found Kaliyah was a "perfectly healthy child" with no significant injuries to suggest that she had been assaulted.

‌



He concluded her cause of death was immersion after water was found in her airways and lungs. The coroner said there was no evidence of anything suspicious related to Kaliyah's death.

Mr Irvine said the other children should not be criticised for not entering the water to rescue Kaliyah, as there is "no Good Samaritan law" in England and Wales. He added that entering the Thames would have been dangerous due to the currents and conditions.

The court heard Kaliyah's family had questions about why they were not informed that the children had left the house to go to the park. Mr Irvine said he understood the family wanted answers but said he was not there to apportion blame. He added: "I know it is not the answer you wanted to hear."

Article continues below

The coroner said allowing children to play without adult supervision was a difficult parenting issue but said there was no criticism from police or safeguarding agencies. He said: "It was at an age where, incrementally, freedom is given to children."

Concluding the inquest, Mr Irvine said: "I very much recognise that my role in this inquest is to be judge. Sometimes, that may come across as stern or uncaring. This is a case that has haunted me from the moment I received it in April 2025. I see this as a tragic accident.

"The circumstances of Kaliyah's death were completely unexpected. The shock that the family must have felt must have seriously impacted their grief. I want to offer my sincere condolences to all of Kaliyah's family and friends. Please accept my condolences."

News.title: Andy Burnham live: Prime Minister to chair first Cabinet meeting after £850m tax cut by scrapping electricity bills VAT
News.content:
Andy Burnham will welcome his appointments round the Cabinet table at No 10 on a day where he hit the ground running by helping millions of UK families with the abolition of VAT on electricity bills

Andy Burnham will chair his first Cabinet meeting soon with the ministers he's appointed in his vow to "bring back hope" to Britain - he began the day helping struggling families by cutting VAT on energy bills.

Burnham started making good on his promise for “breathing space” for struggling households, a key plinth of his economic plans unveiled in his maiden speech outside No 10 on Monday. The move will see VAT removed from domestic electricity bills from October 1.

Burnham said: “Westminster has not been working for people for too long, with families struggling with the cost of living. That needs to change. I said I wanted to give people breathing space, and that’s what I’m announcing on my second day as Prime Minister. We’re taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people’s pockets and bring back hope.”

It is estimated that the change will reduce the annual Ofgem price cap by around £45 from October, with companies expected to pass the reduction onto customers.

Chancellor John Healey said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living. Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter". He continued: “This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”

The fully priced plan from Mr Healey comes as Burnham continues to pad out his cabinet, with a number of key appointments made since yesterday, including Ed Miliband receiving the FCDO brief, Angela Rayner returning as Housing Secretary, and Shabana Mahmood staying on as Home Secretary.

News.title: Tourists flee Barcelona airport as man screams 'jihadist slogans' and throws bag
News.content:
Tourists flee Barcelona airport as man screams 'jihadist slogans' and throws bag

Holidaymakers began running through a terminal at Barcelona Airport to get away after a man shouted and threw a backpack to the ground before he was arrested

View Image The incident occurred at Barcelona-El Prat airport (file) (Image: Quique García/EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock)

A man has sparked terror at Barcelona airport by shouting "jihadist slogans" and throwing a backpack to the ground.

‌



Holidaymakers began running through El Prat airport to get away and at least two people were treated for panic attacks following the drama.

‌



Police called in bomb disposal experts after holding the man with the help of an airport worker.

‌



The Civil Guard’s elite bomb squad TEDAX unit was alerted so they could help ensure the backpack contained no explosives following checks, although sources said this morning they didn’t in the end get involved.

Normality was gradually restored following the scare. The incident occurred around 7.30pm yesterday in the airport’s T2 terminal.

Met Office verdict on August heatwave as weather maps show 37C scorcher READ MORE :

Iran-backed group declares another crucial strait closed as Middle East war widens READ MORE :

The regional Mossos d’Esquadra police force assisted the Civil Guard by mobilising a rapid deployment police tactical unit, which handles complex, high-risk situations across Spain’s Catalan region.

‌



The man responsible for the scare was arrested. Although he was initially described as a Dominican Republic national, police said today he is a 23-year-old from Honduras.

Investigators say they have failed to get a coherent response out of him about why he acted the way he did but have ruled out a terrorist link.

A spokesman for the Civil Guard in Barcelona said this morning: “Witnesses said he suddenly started shouting out jihadist-type slogans at people and officers were called. By the time they reached the scene the suspect had already been neutralised by private airport security staff. We were told he had also assaulted another person but it was a minor assault which didn’t cause any injuries.

‌



“We arrested him on suspicion of a series of crimes including a public order offence and we then determined there was no terror threat despite the nature of what he had been shouting. We took the man to the area where airport medical services are based and they recommended his admission to a psychiatric unit.”

A police source added: “His actions caused a lot of fear among other travellers. Imagine being in an airport and a person starts yelling jihadist-type slogans. It’s normal people get scared. But the response was rapid and it quickly became apparent there was no terrorist threat.”

In March 2019 police in Barcelona arrested a man who reportedly tried to stab several police officers. Respected Spanish newspaper El Pais said he shouted Jihadist slogans after he was detained and told officers he was a ‘messenger’ whose mission was “to kill them all.”

Article continues below

At the start of May a knifeman who stabbed a woman to death in a Barcelona suburb reportedly shouted a similar jihadist comment before targeting his young victim. Pictures of the killer prowling the street before the horror daytime murder went viral.

Locals in Esplugues de Llobregat near Barcelona where the 11am stabbing occurred on May 2 said afterwards they had seen the suspect in the area in the days before the incident. The brutal killing occurred in a residential area near Sant Joan Deu Hospital.

Although initial reports claimed the stab victim was a minor, she turned out to be a 41-year-old Chinese woman. The suspect, a 37-year-old Moroccan, was arrested shortly after the incident.

News.title: 'We live in region where people live longer than anyone else in the UK due to four reasons'
News.content:
'We live in region where people live longer than anyone else in the UK due to four reasons'

One area of the UK has been named as the healthiest place in Britain to grow old, and locals say there are four key reasons which contribute to its remarkable longevity

View 4 Images The ONS crowned the healthiest place in Britain to grow old (Image: Getty Images)

There's one place in the UK putting other places in the country to shame when it comes to the health of its residents.

Earlier this year, a Office for National Statistics study crowned a stunning group of islands as the healthiest place in Britain to grow old. They have the highest average healthspan, which is the age to which you can expect to live in good health.

Orkney, an archipelago off the northeast coast of Scotland, had an incredible average age of 72.9. Other areas in the UK barely got over 60 while in Blackpool, Lancashire, people's health declines after they reach the age of 50.

‌



What is the secret to Orkney's success? According to locals who have lived and breathed the island air off their lives, if there is a secret it is down to four main factors.

Location

The Orkney Islands benefit hugely from its incredible coastlines. Over the last couple of decades, research into so-called Blue Zones has been a hot topic.

They are areas of the world where people living there reportedly have incredible longevity. The designated areas, where many people live beyond 100, are: Okinawa Prefecture in Japan, Nuoro Province in Sardinia, Italy, the Nicoya Peninsula in Costa Rica and Icaria, Greece and Loma Linda in California, USA.

View 4 Images The average healthspan on Orkney is 72.9 (Image: Getty Images)

One thing these places all have in common is that they are either on the coast or very nearby.

There are a number of reasons why living near the coast could boost longevity.

‌



Lesley Palmer, a professor of dementia and ageing design at the University of Stirling, told the I: "The links to the Blue Zones are tempting. There are similarities around resilience [in the face of adverse weather/isolated lives], a lifestyle which encourages natural vigorous movement, purpose, and community.

"And Blue Zones are coastal, with high levels of daylight in the summer months."

Other benefits linked to living by the sea include increased physical activity, stress reduction and cleaner air quality.

‌



Community

Experts are also in agreement that having a sense of community is crucial in living a longer life. When people stop working because they need the money, it is crucial that they still find a sense of purpose.

Atlantic Health reports that having health connections with other people has a huge impact on your long-term health and longevity, and this is another facet that is seen in the Blue Zones - they are generally tight communities.

View 4 Images Locals attribute their longevity to four factors (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Having strong social connections has a huge impact on both physical and mental health - they lower blood pressure, reduce inflammation and improve cardiovascular health. They also provide a buffer against depression, anxiety and other mental health issues.

Community spirit is something available in abundance on Orkney.

Moira Kelday, 70, runs the Stenness Diamond Club, a social group for the over 60s. She told the I: "Community keeps us young. I don't know anybody who just retires. People do volunteering and hobbies."

‌



Exercise

Moving your body is also a crucial component in staying healthier for longer - and this is backed up by the people of Orkney.

Donna Cuthbertson, 41, runs Orkney Dance and Fitness and specialises in teaching older people.

She moved from Maidstone in Kent nine years ago with her husband, a police officer, so is in a position to see how people in Orkney compare to those in other places.

‌



View 4 Images Orkney shares some similarities with Blue Zones (Image: Getty Images)

Donna told the I: "Orkney is good at social connection - everyone looks out for each other.

"They're also good at moving, going out, and even when they retire, they don't stop. They're not just doing cardio, but that muscular, functional movement too."

‌



Experts agree that exercise preserves muscle mass while boosting cardiovascular and brain function.

In Blue Zones, it is common for people to walk to the store and garden by hand.

Food

Lastly, diet is an obvious but important lifestyle aspect that helps people live longer and healthier.

Donna said there is less fast food on the islands with no takeaway delivery services likes Deliveroo and UberEats. There is also no McDonald's, the world's biggest fast food chain. If you're desperate to visit the famous golden arches, you would need to take a ferry or flight to the Scottish mainland.

Donna adds: "Residents are not sitting on the m25, getting home late and putting an oven pizza on. If stress levels are lower then you're eating better."

Blue Zones also have good diets full of fresh ingredients and little or no processed food.

News.title: Three teen killers who stabbed boy, 16, to death on beach in front of girlfriend are jailed
News.content:
Three teen killers who stabbed boy, 16, to death on beach in front of girlfriend are jailed

Kayden Moy, 16, was stabbed to death on a beach in North Ayreshire following an altercation with three teenagers - today all three were jailed for his murder

View 4 Images Kayden Moy, 16 (Image: PA)

Three teenagers have been jailed after a 16-year-old boy was brutally stabbed to death on a beach in North Ayreshire.

‌



Jay Stewart, 19, Cole Turley, 18, and a 15-year-old boy who cannot be named for legal reasons, murdered Kayden Moy, 16, following an altercation on Irvine beach on May 17 2025. Today they were sentenced to a minimum of 16, 16 and 14 years detention respectively.

‌



Turley admitted the killing while Stewart and the 15-year-old were found guilty of murder last month following a trial at the High Court in Glasgow.

‌



All three assailants had been members of the 'Murray Boys' gang in East Kilbride, South Lanarkshire, while Kayden and others were part of the Himshie group in East Kilbride.

Irvine Beach stabbing: How teens at party desperately tried to save Kayden Moy READ MORE :

View 4 Images Kayden was stabbed to death in front of his girlfriend while at Irvine beach in Ayrshire (Image: Facebook)

During the trial the jury heard that shortly before the attack Turley, Stewart, and the 15-year-old had been at the top of a sand dune throwing rocks at people on the beach.

‌



Kayden’s girlfriend Keryn Knox, who had been with him at the beach, said they had been getting ready to leave at about 6pm when the rocks started to be thrown, and Kayden had gone up to confront the teenagers.

Ms Knox told the court: “I went up with him to try and stop him. At that point he had run up the hill and he was just shouting stuff back.

“Then Cole ran in from the side and Kayden has seen a blade and when he tried to run he slipped, and when he tried to get back up Cole has stabbed him in his left lower side twice.”

‌



View 4 Images Killers Jay Stewart and Cole Turley (Image: Police Scotland 2026)

Ms Knox told the court: “His body turned completely white and his limbs were blue and people were crowding round him, trying to put his T-shirt over the wound.”

Another witness said he had gone with Kayden to confront the teenagers, and that as they reached the top of the dune, Turley brought out a knife and Stewart an extendable baton.

‌



The witness said: “Then out of nowhere Cole (Turley) just started running at us. I ran to the right, so did Kayden, I jumped over a grass ledge, Kayden slipped and Cole leaped over and jumped on him.

“He had a knife and it hit. I saw one stab.”

The 16-year-old was so badly injured in the attack that he later died.

‌



Sentencing the three at the same court on Tuesday, judge Lord Scott told them they had gone to the beach that day with the intention of carrying out an attack.

He told them: “Two of you took weapons including, in the case of Cole Turley, the knife with which Kayden Moy was stabbed.”

He added: “You didn’t care whether Kayden lived or died.”

‌



View 4 Images Friends of Kayden paid tribute to the fallen teen following his death

The judge sentenced both Stewart and Turley to a minimum of 16 years in detention, and the 15-year-old to a minimum of 14 years.

Lord Scott also referred to a victim impact statement from Kayden’s family, in which they said they are “devastated beyond words” by his death.

‌



The statement went on: “He was loved beyond measure, and he will be missed for the rest of our lives.”

Prior to the sentencing, Kayden’s father Paul Moy said on social media: “Nothing that happens in that courtroom will ever bring our son back.

“No sentence can fill the emptiness, the heartbreak, or the lifetime of memories we’ve been robbed of.

Article continues below

“Tomorrow is not about closure, because there is no such thing when you lose a child.

“It is about justice, accountability, and making sure my son’s life is remembered.

“Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever my son.”

News.title: Blaenavon wildfire rages with 'close windows' warning as stench smelt 30 miles away
News.content:
Blaenavon wildfire rages with 'close windows' warning as stench smelt 30 miles away

Residents as far as 30 miles away from a major wildfire in Blaenavon, South Wales, have reported smelling strong smoke after a 'change in wind direction overnight'

View 2 Images Residents up to 30 miles away are smelling strong smoke (Image: Ben White)

A major wildfire in Wales has left residents in multiple areas battling a foul stench as fire crews warned them to close their windows.

‌



Several 999 calls were made after the blaze first erupted on Sunday evening in Blaenavon, which covers around 80 hectares of mixed land of bracken and gorse in South Wales.

‌



Residents as far away as Cardiff and Newport have now reported smelling strong smoke due to a "change in wind direction overnight," South Wales Fire and Rescue Service (SWFRS) said.

‌



Crews are continuing to tackle the blaze, with efforts so far hampered by the difficult terrain, access and wind conditions.

The fire service said smoke from the fire could be seen up to 10 miles away and urged residents not to be concerned if they could smell or see it, reports Wales Online.

A SWFRS spokesperson said: "Crews spent the night dealing with a significant wildfire in the Blaenavon area, having received the initial call at 8.42pm on Sunday July 19.

‌



View 2 Images A major wildfire in Blaenavon is ongoing (Image: Ben White)

"This morning, six appliances and a water bowser remain at the scene, supported by SWFRS tactical wildfire officers who are specially trained and highly skilled in responding to these incidents.

"The wildfire currently covers around 80 hectares of mixed land of bracken and gorse. Crews have been working in challenging conditions due to the terrain, access and the wind conditions.

‌



"A change in wind direction overnight has seen smoke from the incident impacting a large area of South Wales, and is reported as far south as Caerphilly and Cardiff. SWFRS is advising anyone affected by this smoke to close their windows and doors.

"SWFRS is receiving a high volume of calls reporting the smoke, however the service would like to reassure communities that they are aware and are dealing with the incident which has caused it. People are being advised to stay away from the area, to allow the emergency response to continue."

People across South Wales including Caerphilly, Newport and Cardiff have also reported smelling strong smoke from the fire.

Article continues below

South Wales Fire and Rescue Service has asked the public not to call to report the smoke unless they believe they have spotted a separate fire. The wildfire remains ongoing.

The fire service is also tackling a separate grass fire in Treherbert, in the South Wales Valleys.

News.title: 24 million homes now under hosepipe ban as Thames Water issues update
News.content:
24 million homes now under hosepipe ban as Thames Water issues update

The UK's biggest water supplier has become the sixth to confirm plans to prevent customers using a hosepipe due to the hot weather and lack of rainfall

View 2 Images Six water companies have now imposed hosepipe bans across parched UK (Image: PA)

Thames Water has announced a hosepipe ban for its 16 million customers after the exceptionally dry hot heather and high demand.

‌



The restriction, also known as a temporary use ban, will come into effect at just after midnight on Thursday.

‌



The UK's biggest water firm is asking households to follow the ban immediately ahead of its official start date. It means customers must not use hosepipes for any non-essential activities, such as watering gardens, cleaning cars, filling paddling pools or topping up hot tubs.

‌



People can still use buckets and watering cans and there are exemptions, including where water use is necessary for health and safety reasons or for customers with severe mobility problems.

Thames gave no indication about how long the ban would be last. It said it will "continue to monitor water levels and conditions" and that restrictions will be lifted as "soon as conditions allow". And it added: "We need prolonged and significant rainfall."

The move by Thames means around 24 million households and businesses will be subject to hosepipe bans across the country. Around eight million already faced being fined for using a hosepipe as supplies react to the ongoing hot weather. On Monday, South East Water became the latest company to announce temporary restrictions for 2.4 million customers in Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire from Saturday, having already had a ban in place in Kent.

‌



Hosepipe bans are enforced by water companies, who have the authority to impose fines of up to £1,000 on those who violate it. Anticipating questions from customers, Thames said: "You don't need to contact us about neighbours using hosepipes. We will get in touch with customers who repeatedly don’t follow the rules. This is to make sure they’re aware of the restrictions and how to use water responsibly." It stressed: "Please do not call 999 if you see someone using a hosepipe."

Thames also confirmed that customers wouldn't be entitled to compensation as a result of the ban and the disruption caused.

The move comes amid speculation that the debt-drenched supplier could be nationalised. The possibility has increased after the arrival of Andy Burnham as PM, given the former Mayor of Manchester has previously backed the idea.

‌



Thames Water said use is currently 10% above normal in the Thames Valley and the Home Counties, as well as 7% above normal in London. The high demand coincides with ongoing hot temperatures that followed three unprecedented heatwaves in three months and the driest spring on record for England and Wales.

View 2 Images Thames Water - with 16 million customers - is by far the biggest supplier to confirm a hosepipe ban this summer (Image: Vuk Valcic/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

‌



Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources at Thames Water, said: "We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment.

"While there is enough water for essential use, we need to reduce non-essential outdoor demand to keep taps flowing. Many customers have already reduced their water use and that support has made a difference. Thank you to everyone who has already changed their daily habits."

Mr Muncaster added that Thames Water teams are working around the clock to keep water moving, fix leaks and support customers.

Article continues below

"We will keep the situation under close review and lift restrictions as soon as it is safe to do so," he added. The ban applies to customers that Thames Water supplies with driving water, but does not apply to waste-only customers or those supplied by another water company.

Thames confirmed the ban a week after its fatcat boss insisted he “deserved” a pay rise to almost £1million despite the firm facing a possible taxpayer rescue. The company’s annual report revealed Chris Weston’s annual salary surged from an already bumper £869,000 to £995,000 from April 1.

News.title: Chris Mason: Starmer ally takes swipe at Burnham's first big policy
News.content:
Whenever there is a reshuffle at the top of government, it is worth keeping an eye and an ear on the dislodged, demoted and rejected former ministers. What do they choose to do and say next?

Andy Burnham has started his first full day in the job with a promise to cut VAT from household electricity bills from 1 October.

But already â within hours - he is taking flak from a man who just yesterday was in a senior job in Downing Street working alongside Sir Keir Starmer.

On Monday night, the former Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, Darren Jones, posted a picture on X of him having a beer, external, captioned "thank you and good night. See you September".

If that was meant to suggest a vow of silence it only lasted a little over 12 hours, because at breakfast time this morning came another post, this one unaccompanied by any picture but loaded with political bite.

"Good news that VAT will be cut on electricity bills," wrote Jones.

"It's a simple way for families to save a few quid, and to mechanically help to keep inflation that little bit lower. But the DigitalID program was unfunded. The government will have to set out how it will pay for its new policies at the budget."

Ouch - that will sting in Downing Street.
