Bayindir, 28, was on World Cup duty with Turkey but did not play in any of their three group stage games.



Turkey failed to progress to the knockout stage and last played on June 26 when they beat the United States.

Bayindir has had his mandatory three-week break but neither he nor Amad will return to United’s Carrington training complex this week.



Tyler Fletcher reported for pre-season last week after remaining an unused substitute in all three of Scotland‘s World Cup games.

Amad played in all four of Ivory Coast’s World Cup games and scored the winner against Ecuador and in the round-of-32 knockout defeat against Norway



Former Fenerbahce ‘keeper Bayindir is expected to return to Turkey, with a move to Besiktas touted.

Bayindir has not played for United since he made another error in their 3-1 defeat at Brentford on September 27.

United lost seven of the 17 games Bayindir started in and he conceded 31 goals.

Ruben Amorim controversially opted to start last season with Bayindir over Andre Onana yet United lost three of their first six Premier League games. Bayindir was culpable for goals in the defeats to Arsenal, Manchester City and Brentford.



Bayindir joined United on transfer deadline day in 2023 for £4.1million but made only one appearance in his first season against League Two Newport County in the FA Cup.

Senne Lammens is firmly established as the United No.1 and the club completed the signing of back-up ‘keeper Karl Darlow last week.

Third choice Tom Heaton signed a new one-year deal and academy goalie Dermot Mee even received a renewal.

Amad and Bayindir would not have been in contention to appear in United’s pre-season friendly against Rosenborg in Norway on Friday had they returned this week.

Sports.title: World Cup 2034 ‘could take place in 2035’ with Fifa facing huge logistical headache amid weather fears
Sports.content:
FIFA are scrambling for ideas as they look ahead to the logistical nightmare presented by the 2034 World Cup.

Saudi Arabia is in line to host in eight years time and, similarly to Qatar, it is expected to be moved to winter – due to extreme weather conditions.



But with the immovable religious calendar and fixed sports dates, the whole schedule could be thrown into disarray.

When their Qatari neighbours hosted in 2022, they held the tournament from November 20 to December 18, so fans will likely be expecting something similar.



They hit a sweet spot in Qatar when they easily avoided the month of Ramadan in April.

In 2034, Ramadan has been projected to begin around November 12 and finish on December 12 as dictated by the Islamic lunar calendar.

During this month, the whole rhythm of Saudi will shift with work and school hours reduced.

By day, the city will be quiet as millions fast and it is customary and respectful to avoid eating, drinking, or smoking in public during these hours.

By night, temporary markets, malls, shops, restaurants all bring life back to the country.

And this could make hosting the World Cup very difficult.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another clash could be seen if they moved it earlier in the year as Salt Lake City’s Winter Olympics are scheduled for January and February.

Then in March, millions of pilgrims will make the journey to Mecca for Hajj.

As the spring approaches, temperatures will begin to soar and Fifa cannot completely throw the rest of the world’s leagues and competitions to the wind.

If the tournament expands to 64 nations, then the tournament will require an even bigger window than this year’s tournament, which had 48 teams.



The hosts need six to seven weeks to stage the tournament over Saudi’s 15 proposed stadiums if it does grow to 64 teams.

They could manage 48 teams at 16 stadiums over around five weeks.

But one sweet spot could be between Christmas 2034 and mid-February 2035 before Hajj.

Weather is going to continue to be an issue for sports scheduling as globalisation continues and climate change becomes more obvious.



In 2025, Fifa president Gianni Infantino explained how even in Europe, July is often “very, very hot”.

On future planning, he said: “We are already into the nitty-gritty, we are discussing all the time.

“It’s not just about one World Cup, it’s a general reflection. The best month to play football, which is June, is not used very much in Europe.

“Maybe there are ways we can optimise the calendar, but we are discussing it and we will see when we come to some conclusions.



“We just have to keep an open mind.”

Another added: “He does not seem to be bothered about the World Cup anymore.”

Ronaldo has not ruled out continuing his international career to the Euros in 2028.



He said: “I’m sad to exit the World Cup like this. But I gave everything. Well, I gave my best. And I leave with a clear conscience.

“This is football, this is the life of a footballer. Sometimes you win, sometimes you lose. And you have to keep going.

“The truth is that it was my last World Cup, yes.

“But now I will have time to think, to be with my family and not to decide things with a hot head. And to continue with life.”

Georgina has been in a relationship with Ronaldo since 2017 after meeting in a Gucci store in Madrid.



The couple have two children together, Alana Martina born in 2017, and Bella Esmeralda born in 2022.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She has also helped to raise Ronaldo’s other three children.

Ronaldo finally popped the question last August with an engagement ring worth a staggering £3.7million.

Sports.title: Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer
Sports.content:
Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer

Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth contract as Manchester United and Arsenal circle, even if the Cherries maintain their midfielder will not be sold

View 2 Images Alex Scott has rejected the offer of a new contract at Bournemouth

Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth deal as the likes of Manchester United circle - but the Cherries stance is set to remain the same.

‌



Scott has received a number of offers since discussions began towards the end of the season, but the Bournemouth midfielder has indicated he is not currently willing to agree new terms, reports Sky Sports.

‌



The 22-year-old has entered the final two years of his deal but the Cherries don't want to sell the Englishman and have rejected enquiries for his signature. As well as the Red Devils; Chelsea and Arsenal have also been linked.

‌



Bournemouth expect Scott to remain their player next season regardless of whether he signs a new deal or continues to run down his contract.

The club, who have just secured European qualification for the first time, have adopted a firm stance as they bid to keep their best players, which also includes Junior Kroupi and winger Rayan, who have attracted plenty of interest.

Man Utd ahead of Arsenal in Manu Kone race after opening transfer talks for £51m star READ MORE :

Scott's stock continued to rise throughout last season and he was selected in his first England squad last November and was then called up into Thomas Tuchel's extended pre-World Cup training camp in Florida.

‌



United are the club most heavily linked with the Bournemouth star given their desire to add to their midfield ranks. They've also prioritised adding Premier League-proven talent, but reports claim their attention has shifted to Manu Kone, the Roma midfielder who was hugely impressive for France at the World Cup.

View 2 Images Alex Scott's displays earned him England recognition

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023 for £25m and they would be able to demand a fee that far exceeds that if they did want to cash in. In recent years the Cherries have been prepared to sell their top assets for huge profits, but are determined to retain them this summer.

Article continues below

Midway through last season they sold Antoine Semenyo to Manchester City for £65m. That came after a summer where they cashed in on Milos Kerkez, who headed for Liverpool, and Dean Huijsen to Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Fake football shirt fire warning after £18m of counterfeit kits seized in UK during World Cup
Sports.content:
Fake football shirt fire warning after £18m of counterfeit kits seized in UK during World Cup

The tournament saw a spike in the sales of fake shirts amid warnings they are more flammable than the real deal as fans hit out at the sky high prices for Premier League teams' shirts

True Cost of Football Investigation: Fans face highest-on-record prices for tickets and shirts

Counterfeit football shirts worth over £18m were seized in the UK during the World Cup due to safety concerns.

‌



The tournament produced a spike in the sales of fake shirts and kits, but the Fire Service has warned that these items are far more flammable and dangerous than the genuine articles. The seizures came as fans hit out at the sky high prices charged for Premier League teams' replica shirts and the new England kit.

‌



More than 220,000 pieces of football merchandise were recovered by the Police Intellectual Property Office as part of Operation Bloxwich, a UK police enforcement effort targeting counterfeit goods. Border Force officers snatched more than 1,000 shirts and were working ‘round-the-clock’ to stop ‘thousands more’ from flooding the streets before the World Cup. The seized shirts were recovered in at least 23 separate operations.

‌



View 2 Images Counterfeit shirts seized during the tournament were worth millions of pounds (Image: City of Edinburgh Council)

Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans READ MORE :

Huge World Cup 2030 change already confirmed as football chief 'leaks' announcement READ MORE :

Investigators said the shirts contained harmful chemicals banned under UK safety laws that could pose a ‘particular risk to children. Some had dangerous levels of poisons such as arsenic and lead. Other anti-counterfeit units confiscated up to 15,000 bogus shirts in the World Cup run-up. A Border Force spokesman said wearing the fake gear could harm children.

“Seized shirts have been found to contain harmful chemicals banned under UK safety law - a particular risk for children,” the spokesman added. “There is no quality check, no safety guarantee, and no recourse if something goes wrong.

‌



“While shoppers looking may be looking for a bargain, they are inadvertently supporting illegal and criminal activities, fuelling child and forced labour. The dangerous underground economy fake shirts support can include drug smuggling, serious violence and dangerous working conditions.”

View 2 Images Counterfeit shirts seized earlier this year (Image: City of Edinburgh Council)

The Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit at the City of London force seized more than 4,000 bogus shirts in April alone. One raid involved 1,618 fake strips being taken from a warehouse in Birmingham, including replicas of star players such as France's Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland.

‌



Det Sgt Jamie Kirk, who took part in the operation, said: "I understand why people want to buy these shirts, people love football and the incentive is the lower price - but these shirts, they're not regulated and could be highly flammable. They have dyes in them which could be harmful to skin, particularly children's skin. While the cost is lower - and that's the attractive part - potential damages to you and the people making them is just far too high."

Cheshire Fire and Rescue Service tested the flammability of counterfeit shirts compared with genuine kit and found the fake kits were much more flammable. W atch manager Dave Jackson said: "It's quite clear that the counterfeit one melted as soon as the burner went on it."

He carried out the test by hanging them two at a time on an iron bar and used blow torches to set them alight. He added: "I really had to try to make the genuine one ignite and melt."

‌



One of the factors driving the sales of counterfeit kits is their low price. T hey are sold online for £12, while the cost of some official Premier League strips start at £85.

"It's extremely dangerous. It's something that can cause horrific injuries to your children. It's just not worth the savings," Jackson added. Kate Caffrey, head of intelligence at the Intellectual Property Office, warned that fake shirts are not regulated.

"Counterfeit strips are not subject to health and safety regulations, British Standards [or] EU standards," she said. "We've got evidence that counterfeit goods are made in appalling conditions.

Article continues below

"So you just don't know what's in them, how they're being made and there's no way of providing any safety reassurances. Counterfeiting is criminal, these are manufactured and supplied by criminal networks, criminal gangs.

"They're very adept at targeting markets where there's demand. So the World Cup, the forthcoming Premier League season - they're going to flood the market with fake shirts. The price of a fake shirt, you don't know what you're funding with that money."

Border Force director general Phil Douglas said: ”Criminals are deliberately exploiting fans' passion for the game. Our officers are working around the clock to stop them. We are protecting fans from being ripped off." He added that the aim was to "keep illegal goods out of the UK.”

Sports.title: England's insane starting XI for World Cup 2030 that will make us hot favourites
Sports.content:
England's insane starting XI for World Cup 2030 that will make us hot favourites

England's next opportunity for global glory will come at the World Cup 2030

View 13 Images England have a tremendous wealth of talent in years to come (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

England's chances to end 60 years of hurt went undone at the World Cup 2026. The Three Lions were eliminated in the semi-finals by Argentina but managed their best finish at the tournament since 1966.

‌



Their thrilling 6-4 victory over France ensured they finished third with Spain claiming the ultimate victory after besting Lionel Messi and co in the final. Attention has now shifted to Euro 2028 with Thomas Tuchel's side's next chance to lift the World Cup set to come in 2030.

‌



The tournament, which will be jointly-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, will not be attended by Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo who announced that this summer was their last appearance in a World Cup. Four years can result in new stars being born and current ones losing steam as Mirror Football looks at what could England's starting XI in 2030...

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

All 37 World Cup pundits ranked as BBC vs ITV winner decided and unexpected star emerges READ MORE :

John Cross’ alternative World Cup awards as FIFA bosses called out for huge mistake READ MORE :

James Trafford

View 13 Images James Trafford is currently back-up for club and country (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Age is on the side of James Trafford who'll be 27 years of age in 2030. Current number one Jordan Pickford will be 36 years old but club form will be imperative for Trafford should he aim to usurp the Everton icon.

‌



Trafford is number two at Manchester City given the existence of Gianluigi Donnarumma. However, displacing the Italian in years to come - or leaving the Etihad Stadium - could allow the talented goalkeeper to play week in, week out and prove he can star for his country.

Tino Livramento

View 13 Images The Newcastle star was forced to miss out on the World Cup due to injury (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Injuries might be the only factor impacting Tino Livramento's chance of becoming England's first-choice right-back. The Newcastle ace pulled out of the World Cup squad due to injury in what preceded chaos at the position with Reece James also getting injured and Jarell Quansah being sent off against Mexico.

‌



The 23-year-old is an all-round footballer at full-back and provides unbelievable energy on both sides of the ball. If he gets over his injury issues, Livramento can call the right-back role for England home for years to come.

Marc Guehi

View 13 Images Marc Guehi impressed at the tournament (Image: 2026 FIFA)

The Manchester City defender enjoyed a good tournament and played an integral role in England's run to the semi-finals. The 26-year-old's poise and intelligence was important for Tuchel's side and will no doubt continue his run in the side four years from now.

‌



Ayden Heaven

View 13 Images Ayden Heaven has yet to make his England debut (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

The Manchester United centre-back played 18 games for the Red Devils last season and impressed despite being just 19 years of age. The defender's best attributes are his composure and ball-carrying from the back.

With John Stones likely to have played his last World Cup, opportunities to assert himself in the conversations to be a starter for England are available. Defenders in modern football are expected to control the tempo of a game from deep and with Heaven excelling at that, he could very well emerge to be an important figure for his nation in four years.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lewis Hall

View 13 Images Lewis Hall has become an integral player for Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

The absence of Lewis Hall from Tuchel's squad came as a surprise to many, especially given the lack of natural left-backs in his squad. The 21-year-old has become an important player for Eddie Howe at Newcastle with his accuracy from crosses and playmaking ability making him among the best full-backs in the country.

‌



Alex Scott

View 13 Images Alex Scott could replace Declan Rice in the starting lineup (Image: Getty)

While Alex Scott remains without an England cap, the Bournemouth midfielder joined the national team camp for their World Cup preparation earlier this summer and was seriously considered for a place in the squad.

The 22-year-old differs from Declan Rice in his excellent technical ability and his capability of keeping the ball in tight spaces. The Arsenal talisman endured a disappointing campaign in which he carried a back injury and suffered with illness.

‌



Scott will receive further opportunities to impress for England as his penchant of keeping calm in the most congested area of the pitch could be a quality Tuchel has earmarked for 2030.

Elliot Anderson

View 13 Images Elliot Anderson was a constant in Thomas Tuchel's midfield (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester City's £116million man was ever-present for Tuchel this summer. Elliot Anderson formed a strong midfield duo alongside Declan Rice in what was the 23-year-old's first major tournament for England.

‌



His move to Manchester will only improve him on the pitch with the opportunity to play Champions League football alongside the best players in Europe can only spell good news for England's future.

Max Dowman

View 13 Images Max Dowman is still 16 years old (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Currently representing England U19s, Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman is already one of the brightest young talents in Europe. With 13 appearances for the Gunners already under his belt, the experience and opportunities he'll gain in the next few years under Mikel Arteta will no doubt mark a pathway to become an important player for England.

‌



His team-mates in Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke shared duties at right-wing in North America with neither player impressing enough to stamp their authority on the position. Saka's recent injury issues and his move more central on the pitch under Arteta could free up space for Dowman on the right.

Jude Bellingham

View 13 Images Jude Bellingham scored six goals at the World Cup (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Perhaps the most obvious player on this list, Jude Bellingham is already circling conversations of being England's best player ever and he turned 23 just last month. The Real Madrid superstar will be in his prime in 2030 at 27 years of age and will likely be captain if for the absence of Harry Kane.

‌



The midfielder is the present and future of England and provides them the X-factor that all top teams have with their best player.

Rio Ngumoha

View 13 Images Rio Ngumoha could call the left-wing spot his own in 2030 (Image: getty)

The Liverpool starlet made his England debut in their pre-tournament friendly against New Zealand and received the Player of the Match award. Expected to have an increased role for his club under Andoni Iraola this season, the 17-year-old simply doesn't have a limit on his otherworldly talent.

‌



The left-wing spot certainly isn't clamped down by one player in particular with Anthony Gordon and Marcus Rashford sharing the duties this summer, although the former was preferred in the knockout stages.

Ngumoha has the opportunity to stake his claim on the position for the next decade and more and will no doubt be eyeing 2030 as his chance to make his tournament debut for his country.

Harry Kane

View 13 Images Harry Kane will be 36 years old by the time of the next World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The England captain will be 36 years old in 2030 but given his game continues to rely less on pace and athleticism, there's a chance the Bayern Munich striker can represent his country in what would be his fourth, and likely final, World Cup.

After the Three Lions were eliminated by Argentina, Kane refused to rule out his possible appearance in four years. He said: "I think you know me as a person by now. I'm coming off my best season ever, and I'm 32, nearly 33.

"It's impossible to say; four years is obviously a long way away. Playing for England is my biggest ambition, my proudest thing to do. I feel as good as I've ever felt. Let's see. As long as I'm performing, I'll be representing England. That's just the way it is."

Sports.title: Full list of Argentina's 11 biggest World Cup controversies as punishments emerge
Sports.content:
Full list of Argentina's 11 biggest World Cup controversies as punishments emerge

Argentina were at the centre of controversial scenes after the World Cup final and the team were involved in several other incidents during the tournament

View 6 Images Argentina's Leandro Paredes was involved in ugly post-match scenes at the World Cup final (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Argentina ended their World Cup campaign with disgraceful scenes after the final whistle. The country’s reign as world champions was ended by Spain’s 1-0 victory on Sunday.

‌



They had attempted to stifle their opponents and didn't register a shot until the 117th minute after they had been undone by Ferran Torres’ strike in extra-time. Several Argentine stars’ reactions to the result led to embarrassing post-match scenes, which are under investigation by FIFA.

‌



A statement read: “Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FIFA disciplinary code with regard to the post-match incidents.”

‌



In addition to violent conduct, the disciplinary and ethics prosecutor will help the investigation determine whether Argentina breached Article 13 of the disciplinary code, regarding offensive behaviour and principles of fair play. Serious breaches have previously led to lengthy suspensions, which could apply to any Argentina players or staff found to have broken the rules.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spanish Football Federation president Luis Rubiales was given a three-year ban for kissing Jenni Hermoso after the Women's World Cup final. Luis Suarez was also infamously given a four-month ban for biting Giorgio Chiellini at the World Cup 2014. Argentina were already under investigation before the World Cup final, with a long list of controversies following them through the tournament.

‌



Cristian Romero issues statement after World Cup final loss and vile Argentina scenes READ MORE :

Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

World Cup final scenes

Midfielder Leandro Paredes, whose reported post-match red card has been removed from FIFA’s records, pushed Spain defender Eric Garcia's throat before kicking him. He was also involved in a confrontation with Gavi, whom he grabbed before pushing him to the ground.

View 6 Images Paredes was widely condemned for his actions and could be set for a lengthy ban (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The post-match scenes appeared to start after Argentina defender Nahuel Molina seemingly struck Spain skipper Rodri in the stomach. The Manchester City midfielder had run on the pitch to celebrate with his team-mates but stopped to confront Molina after the incident.

‌



Further controversy has since emerged, as footage showed Argentina legend and current assistant coach Roberto Ayala appearing to throw a punch at Spain's Dani Olmo after the game. These three moments have overshadowed the World Cup final and Argentina were involved in several other contentious incidents during the tournament.

Messi and Mac Allister escape punishment

Lionel Messi kick-started his World Cup with a hat-trick against Algeria but the Argentine icon was arguably fortunate to still be on the pitch shortly after his opening goal. The veteran forward appeared to plant his studs on the right leg of opposition defender Aissa Mandi.

View 6 Images Lionel Messi escaped punishment for a foul against Algeria (Image: Omar Vega/Getty Images)

‌



Messi did not receive a yellow card for the challenge from Polish referee Szymon Marciniak, while VAR did not intervene as it was not deemed a red card offence.

Algeria subsequently lodged a complaint over alleged poor refereeing. Their complaint also highlighted an incident involving Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister, who also went unpunished after catching Ibrahim Maza in the face with his elbow in the 74th minute.

Mac Allister incident vs Austria

Mac Allister found himself at the centre of discussions in Argentina’s second group game against Austria. Messi opened the scoring in a 2-0 win, overtaking Miroslav Klose’s record for World Cup goals.

‌



However, his record-breaking strike arguably should not have stood. Replays appeared to show Mac Allister fouling Austria's Xaver Schlager to win possession for Argentina in the build-up to the goal, but VAR did not intervene.

View 6 Images Mac Allister was alleged to have committed a foul in the lead-up to a goal against Austria (Image: Pablo Morano/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

Egypt controversies

Argentina required a remarkable comeback to produce a 3-2 victory over Egypt in the round of 16. However, Egypt felt their hopes of progressing to the quarter-finals had been hampered by two refereeing decisions.

‌



The Pharaohs saw a goal controversially ruled out following VAR intervention. Upon review, referee Francois Letexier judged that Marwan Ateya had fouled Lisandro Martinez at the start of Egypt’s attacking move at the other end of the pitch.

However, late in the game, Egypt were denied a penalty for an alleged foul on Mohamed Salah shortly before Argentina’s winning goal. Egypt filed a complaint to FIFA over the two decisions and manager Hossam Hassan made his thoughts clear.

He said: "Why isn't there any fairness in sport? In football? I do not want to try to put it nicely here with beautiful wording. We have been treated unfairly today. We have suffered injustice."

‌



View 6 Images Egypt manager Hossam Hassan was unhappy with the referee's decisions against Argentina (Image: Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

Mistaken identity

Argentina benefited from one of the new rules implemented at the World Cup during their quarter-final win over Switzerland. Portuguese referee Joao Pinheir had initially shown Paredes a yellow card.

However, that decision was reversed under the new ‘mistaken identity’ rule after footage showed that Breel Embolo had dived, with the card awarded to the Swiss forward instead. Unfortunately for Embolo, he had already been booked and was sent off during a crucial match in bizarre circumstances.

‌



There were question marks raised over the use of the mistaken identity rule in this scenario, which changed the offence from a foul by Paredes to simulation by Embolo. UEFA has since instructed its officials not to deem potential simulations as mistaken identity cases. UEFA believes mistaken identity should apply to factual decisions, be applied to the same offence and not require on-field reviews, while simulation is a subjective call that would require referees to re-examine the incident.

England incidents

England suffered a semi-final defeat to Argentina after succumbing to two late goals. Away from the questions raised over Thomas Tuchel’s tactics, the game was marred by two notable post-match incidents.

‌



View 6 Images Argentina celebrated with the banner after defeating England (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

During Argentina’s celebrations on the pitch, several players held up a banner that read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine).” A reference to the British overseas territory and the 1982 Falklands War, FIFA is investigating the incident and Argentinian officials are reportedly expecting a fine of $20,000.

After the final whistle, Jude Belligham was also seen confronting Argentina’s Valentin Barco. Bellingham appeared to slap Barco but the exact reason for the flashpoint is unknown.

‌



Barco had antagonised England players earlier in the match with his celebrations for Argentina's winning goal. After the final whistle, Bellingham had shaken hands with an Argentine player before spotting Barco joining a group of his team-mates and exchanging words with the defender.

Sports.title: Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool all facing nine-figure transfer problem this summer
Sports.content:
It could very well prove to be the transfer window that shatters the record £3billion spending spree that engulfed Premier League clubs last summer.

Because although deals may not yet be coming thick and fast, the outlays have been significant. Transfer activity among Premier League clubs should accelerate following the conclusion of the World Cup, which was always likely to hamper the more substantial deals involving the biggest stars. And yet, three nine-figure deals have already been struck.

Elliot Anderson was the first domino to fall. Courted by both Manchester clubs, it was Manchester City who agreed to part with £116million to make the 23-year-old midfielder the most expensive British footballer in history.

As it turns out, Anderson did not hold that title for long; Chelsea have since agreed to pay £117m for Morgan Rogers, who finalised his move to Stamford Bridge on Monday. In between those deals, Tottenham signed off a £100m package to lure Sandro Tonali to London.

‌



Since Jack Grealish became the first £100m transfer in Premier League history back in 2021, seven others have joined him in that club.

Never before, though, have three £100m-plus deals happened in a single transfer window — until now. And it is likely more will follow before the September 1 deadline.

Even though others have so far abstained from parting with such astronomical sums, the deals for Anderson and Rogers in particular will distort the market. Once a new level in transfer fees has been met, those sums will be seized upon by clubs as the new benchmark in the market.

That is something Arsenal have already discovered this summer. It's understood that they would have maybe gone to £80m to land Rogers: a figure which may have got a deal done prior to the World Cup. However, Anderson's mega move to Manchester City led to Aston Villa increasing their valuation of the attacking midfielder over the course of the summer.

‌



Indeed, two more of Arsenal's priority transfer targets this summer, Bradley Barcola and Julian Alvarez, are valued in excess of £100m, making those prospective deals difficult unless the Gunners are willing to smash their previous record outlay.

View 3 Images Manchester City agreed to pay £116m to bring Elliot Anderson to The Etihad

Arsenal are known to be resolute in sticking to their valuations of targets, hence why they were unwilling to match Chelsea in their pursuit of Rogers. Even if they pivot to alternative targets, they are unlikely to be cheap given the standard of player they will be in the market for after winning the Premier League. If they are to truly level up their attack, it almost feels inevitable that they will have to break the £100m barrier again after doing so to sign Declan Rice previously.

Liverpool are also admirers of Barcola and need to acquire a successor to Mohamed Salah, who brought the curtain down on his legendary Anfield career at the end of the 2025-26 campaign. They do have form for nine-figure splurges, spending £116m to bring Florian Wirtz to Anfield last summer and then a further £125m on Alexander Isak. Both deals represented British record transfer fees, with Isak surpassing Wirtz weeks later.

‌



Again, the calibre of Liverpool's targets means they are likely to be shopping in the nine-figure price bracket this year. Yan Diomande, a player they were keen on earlier in the summer, was valued at £110.4m by RB Leipzig, though a move to Paris Saint-Germain now looks more likely.

Manchester United are the Premier League heavyweight yet to be dragged into paying a nine-figure fee for a player. Furthermore, they will feel they have found value in a vastly inflated market after finalising deals for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans for £50m and £35m respectively.

View 3 Images Arsenal and Liverpool will likely have to pay in excess of £100m if they are to land Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

The Red Devils are still in the market for one more midfielder plus reinforcements in other areas and even though it feels unlikely they will break the £100m barrier, the state of the market will effect them too.

‌



United have continued to target established Premier League players after successful moves for Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha last season, but even deals for those players outside the elite bracket are soaring. Alex Scott of Bournemouth, a player admired by both United and Arsenal, would likely cost in excess of £80m. If a deal were to be done at that level, it would make the 22-year-old the joint-third biggest transfer acquisition in United's history.

That Premier League premium, if you will, has already been seen across other deals. Matheus Fernandes, for example, was another serious target for Manchester United and was sold by relegated West Ham to Tottenham for a staggering £85m: a price United were simply unwilling to met.

The trajectory of the market leaves United and other Premier League clubs in a difficult spot when it comes to their mission to strengthen their respective squads over the remainder of the summer transfer window

With transfer fees continuing to ascend that an extreme rate, it seems like the market is only heading one way. And unless they can get very creative, then the majority of clubs will have to move along with it.

‌

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red

Argentina star Leandro Paredes has spoken out following his violent outburst after the World Cup final against Spain where he appeared to attack some of the victors

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes reacted violently (Image: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Argentina star Leandro Paredes, who violently attacked Spain's stars following the World Cup final, has boldly chosen to not apologise for his actions. The midfielder has instead expressed pride in his side's efforts during the tournament in his first statement following the incident

‌



Paredes was spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, interrupting Spain's celebrations. Nauel Molina appeared to instigate the violent altercation by throwing a punch at Manchester City star Rodri.

‌



During the post-match drama, it was claimed that Paredes was shown a red card for his actions. However, the red card was removed from the record, and FIFA took no disciplinary action, according to BBC Sport.

‌



No apology was forthcoming in Paredes first public words following the chaos.

Paredes wrote: "Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves.

Cristian Romero issues statement after World Cup final loss and vile Argentina scenes READ MORE :

Argentina fans go wild as pilot tells them they've won World Cup in brutal prank READ MORE :

"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team.

‌



"To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

While a red card is not on record, FIFA have confirmed that they will investigate what took place.

A statement read: ”Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (FDC), the FIFA Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents."

While on BBC's commentary for the final, Alan Shearer said: "Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them. There is no place or space for that.

‌



"We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Sports.title: FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card
Sports.content:
FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card

FIFA is taking action against Argentina - but a red card previously issued in the World Cup final at MetLife Stadium has been wiped from the records

Spain celebrate World Cup triumph with open-top bus parade

FIFA has launched an investigation into potential disciplinary breaches by Argentina following their World Cup final defeat to Spain. The world governing body has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to examine the incidents that unfolded after Sunday's game at MetLife Stadium.

‌



Several Argentina players and coaching staff members could now face severe sanctions if found guilty, while the Argentine Football Association (AFA) also risks another financial penalty. A statement from FIFA confirmed: “Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

‌



“Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.”

‌



The South Americans were again criticised over their physical approach during their 1-0 defeat, with Enzo Fernandez sent off for two bookable offences towards the end of normal time. Then, after the game, Nahuel Molina struck Rodri in the chest as he ran past him celebrating, and Argentina’s assistant coach Roberto Ayala was then involved in an altercation with Dani Olmo.

Leandro Paredes also appeared to have been sent off following the full-time whistle after grabbing Spain defender Eric Garcia by the throat. However, the dismissal was later removed from FIFA's official records, with the governing body later confirming that no disciplinary action had actually been taken against the midfielder during the aftermath of the match.

Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Leandro Paredes hits Gavi following the World Cup final (Image: (Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images))

As a result, any suspension or sanction for him would arise from any retrospective investigation that may be opened by the FIFA disciplinary committee. FIFA also last week confirmed it is assessing reports from the semi-final against England following the controversy surrounding the Falkland Islands.

He has since broken his silence on social media, but failed to apologise for his part in the fracas. Paredes said: "Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves.

‌



"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team.

"To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

After beating Thomas Tuchel’s side 2-1, Argentina players celebrated with a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' - 'The Falklands are Argentine'. Players including Tottenham defender Cristian Romero, former Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso and Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez could also potentially face individual sanctions for displaying the banner.

‌



View 2 Images Argentina celebrated wit the banner after defeating England (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Speaking after the final, former England international Joe Hart labelled Argentina’s behaviour 'disgusting'. He said: “There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players. The game’s done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened. Disgusting behaviour.”

While Wayne Rooney added: “Does it surprise you? It doesn’t surprise me. We’ve seen this with Argentina before. It’s just not the reaction you want.

‌



"We’ve seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That’s just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It’s really poor from them.”

But Lionel Scaloni, the Argentina head coach, claimed after the game: “We are gracious in victory, and we must be gracious in defeat. Today, we are showing that we know how to lose. We lost the match and we accept it, but that doesn’t mean we stop living or forget everything we did to get here."

Sports.title: Charges and challenges - the scale of the task facing Maresca at Man City
Sports.content:
Plenty of the Premier League's top clubs have rolled the managerial dice ahead of next season. Manchester City are one of those starting a new era, turning to Enzo Maresca in the wake of Pep Guardiola's decision to depart.

Maresca is returning for his third stint at the club, having been an academy coach in 2020-21 and then Guardiola's assistant in 2022-23 - the famous Premier League-Champions League-FA Cup treble-winning campaign.

He is familiar with the pursuit of silverware, but is yet to be the one to deliver it at such scale. So, how well positioned is he to lead Man City to glory in 2026-27?

Sky Sports' Ben Ransom and Laura Hunter explore Maresca's chances of success in year one - and whether trophies are the only barometer by which he will be judged in the wake of Guardiola's seismic exit.

Sympathetic start gives Maresca breathing room

Maresca has been given a kind start to his term, meeting Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Coventry City in his first three outings - a generous run to be able to establish some early rhythm. It also gives Man City's World Cup warriors, those in battle until the very last, a chance to ease back in.

Image: Rodri played nearly every minute of Spain's World Cup campaign

Rodri played nearly every minute of Spain's triumphant campaign and is the most susceptible to breaking down with fatigue. Given those first three fixtures will still heavily favour Man City without him, he should benefit from a phased return.

Maresca will, however, be under pressure to deliver given how winnable those fixtures are on paper. He cannot afford to cede ground early, especially as City face Man Utd and Liverpool in two of the next three in September. Clearly both of those rival bouts hold significance beyond the result.

As the Italian acknowledged when joining, he is in a "dream situation", inheriting a well-balanced squad with incredible talent and depth, built by Guardiola. "It provides the consistency I need to do my job effectively," he said.

The demands will therefore be the same as what were placed on Guardiola, without necessarily having the unique job security the Spaniard was afforded. Guardiola always managed on his own terms. Maresca has a strong bond with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, but won't necessarily get the same privilege.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports football journalist Laura Hunter says Enzo Maresca won't be afforded time to excel as Manchester City boss

How much time will players need to adapt?

In terms of style, it's not quite rinse and repeat but there are plenty of similarities between Maresca and Guardiola's preferred way of playing.

Both are rooted in possessing the ball, favouring control, and pressing aggressively. Maresca is arguably more expansive, though, wanting to stretch the pitch with wingers that play high and wide.

Image: Chelsea's stats in their only full season under Enzo Maresca

City's wingers have been coached more recently to play a style where they tuck inside and rotate to create central overloads. Most of the play revolves around Rodri, but it's fluid.

Watching City under Guardiola often meant seeing defenders step into midfield, midfielders become forwards, or even drop into full-back. Maresca's more rigid 4-2-3-1 structure will likely make for more traditional roles.

It also requires a high-functioning No 10 to link play. At Chelsea, that was Cole Palmer. Maresca has got Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki to choose between, should he wish to adopt the same setup here.

How is the squad shaping up?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom explains why Manchester City decided to sign Elliot Anderson for £116m, making him the most expensive British player in history

There has been a concerted effort over the past two or three transfer windows under Hugo Viana to lower the average age of the squad. It's dropped from 29 to just over 25, albeit a leadership void has appeared following the departures of Bernardo Silva and John Stones this summer - and Kevin de Bruyne before them.

Rodri and Ruben Dias are important, while last season saw City lean further into a leadership role for Erling Haaland. Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol are also experienced, stable figures, plus Mateo Kovacic. The spine of the team remains incredibly strong.

Business to date has been costly but smart. Elliot Anderson, signed for mega money from Nottingham Forest, has been bought to add robustness and future-proof midfield and young Jeremy Monga has been poached from Leicester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Rodri linked with a move away from Manchester City, Sky Sports News reporter Ben Ransom discusses whether Ayyoub Bouaddi could be brought in to replace the midfielder

The wish list also includes a right-back and a winger, while keeping tabs on Lille teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi, who excelled at the World Cup for Morocco. Arsenal are also admirers of him.

Depending on potential suitors meeting the club's valuation, outgoings might comprise a selection of: Savinho, Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, Jack Grealish, Tijjani Reijnders and Rico Lewis. Transfer activity is expected to accelerate now the World Cup has concluded.

What are Maresca's main challenges?

This is the first time since the Abu Dhabi takeover that the plan is uncertain. 10 years ago, all preparation went into building a club to lure Guardiola to the Premier League. That vision has been and gone, so where now?

City have forged a culture geared towards winning silverware, anything less is unlikely to be tolerated for a sustained period. Fans arrive at the Etihad expecting to be entertained, but above all, demanding to win. Balancing both is where Maresca's Chelsea failed.

The 46-year-old does have the benefit of not being the only managerial newbie at one of the top clubs, though, making for a changeable Premier League landscape as the natural order figures itself out. At City, that is being viewed as an opportunity to take advantage of.

Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso at Chelsea and, perhaps to a lesser extent, Michael Carrick at Man Utd, all hold question marks. This era of unknowns is fertile ground for anyone with ambition to make a mark. Very much sink or swim.

What about the 115 charges?

115 Premier League charges still cloud the club. Maresca will have to field difficult questions from the media over it.

Guardiola was the master of public-facing confrontation, having had to handle media glare at some of Europe's biggest clubs all his career. He knew the City press pack well and how to shut down any exchanges he wished not to speak on.

Maresca came under fire at Chelsea at times but mainly over football matters. How he handles this situation will likely impact his first 12 months - assuming a verdict is reached within that timeframe.

Maresca is due to give his first Man City press conference on Friday, July 24. You can follow everything that is said in our dedicated live blog here.

Sports.title: 'Fery can improve but that's exciting' - Henman optimistic as Brit eyes US Open run
Sports.content:
British No 1 Arthur Fery will head into the American hard-court swing with areas he can improve ahead of the US Open - but that's "exciting", says Tim Henman.

The wild card's surprise run to the Wimbledon semi-finals has injected a much-needed shot of positivity and given British fans a new name to follow in the Grand Slams - starting at the US Open in New York - live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30.

The challenge for the 24-year-old now is to acclimatise to his new standing in the game and the loss of anonymity and the freedom that brings with it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery reflects on his Wimbledon experience, his massive climb up the world rankings and the tournaments he's planning to play next

The 23-year-old, who has soared to 36 in the world from No 114, was the last player standing in what was an otherwise dismal tournament for the host nation, but he became only the fifth British man this century to reach the second week at the All England Club.

Fery has earned direct entry to a Masters event for the first time in Cincinnati - 13-23 August - before appearing at the Winston-Salem Open from 23-29 August ahead of his debut at Flushing Meadows.

Speaking at Royal Birkdale ahead of The Open, Henman called Fery's dream run at the All England Club "amazing" and "transformational for his career and his life".

The former British No 1 said: "He started the year at 185 in the world, qualified in Melbourne and then has continued to improve his ranking - then getting a wild card at Wimbledon ranked 114 and winning five matches getting to the semi-finals it was an incredible performance - and I think it also shows the fine margins between these top players.

"If you're in the top 250 in the world you're an extremely good player and on your day you've got a chance of beating anyone, so huge for him to be 36 in the world now getting to the other Grand Slams and Masters 1000, so he's got an opportunity to really plan his schedule moving forward."

"I mean it's interesting that actually the ranking points will come on after Wimbledon and then the entries are six weeks out so I think the first tournament he will take advantage of that is Cincinnati," explained Henman.

The 2004 US Open semi-finalist also believes Fery will only improve his overall power in order to compete with top-tier opponents.

"Yes, even already a little bit during the tournament I was thinking of life after and how I was going to handle all that because we've seen it with people who've broken through in that manner before," Fery told Sky News' Jacquie Beltrao.

"With Emma obviously, Emma won a Slam and I didn't but there was still a lot of media attention.

"It is going to be really important to handle that - the expectation from myself and also the public."

The Brit is ready for more time in the media glare as he competes against the top players in tennis.

"It means I can play the top players week in week out and compare myself to them and keep working on my tennis," said Fery.

"I am going to have to get accustomed to the full life of tour with more media attention and all of that but I think I'm ready for it.

Sports.title: Arsenal, Chelsea and Man Utd target Scott rejects new Bournemouth contract
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth contract amid strong interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, Sky Sports News understands.

Bournemouth have made Scott a number of offers since discussions began towards the end of the season - but it is believed the midfielder has indicated he is not currently willing to agree new terms.

The Cherries do not want to sell the talented midfielder, who has entered the final two years of his current contract, and have already knocked back inquiries from the Premier League trio.

United, Chelsea and Arsenal are believed to remain the frontrunners for Scott, who travelled to the States with the England squad ahead of the World Cup, while other clubs are also keen.

Bournemouth expect Scott to remain their player next season whether he signs a new offer or continues on his current deal.
