Sports.title: When does the summer transfer window shut? Deadline day info amid spending spree
Sports.content:
When does the summer transfer window shut? Deadline day info amid spending spree

The summer transfer window is well underway, with big-money business being completed left, right and centre.

But clubs are going to have to make sure they get all of their signings over the line by the time the deadline comes around.



2 Santos to Man United has been one of the biggest deals of the summer Credit: Getty

Already this summer, there have been multiple record-breaking £100million-plus transfers made in the Premier League.

Elliot Anderson has joined Manchester City, Sandro Tonali has signed for Tottenham and Morgan Rogers is set for Chelsea.

However, time will feel like it's quickly running out for all clubs to get their deals done as the deadline gets closer...



When does the transfer window shut?

The transfer deadline in England is set for Tuesday, September 1.

For the last two windows, the closing time was set for 7pm, but the time will now return to its original later deadline.

It means the summer window closes at 11pm on September 1.

Clubs can submit deal sheets before the deadline to give themselves a two-hour grace period to complete transfers.



This deadline is in place for the Premier League and EFL.

In the WSL, the window closes at 11pm on Thursday, September 3.

And that's the same day as the Scottish Premiership, but in Scotland, the deadline is going to be set for 5pm rather than 11pm.

2 England star Anderson has joined Man City for a record-breaking fee Credit: Getty



When is the deadline across Europe?

For LaLiga clubs, their summer window shuts at a similar time to in England, with the deadline set for September 1 at 10:59pm.

In Italy and Serie A, clubs have until 8pm on the same day.

As for the Bundesliga, their deadline is Monday, August 31 at 7pm.

When does the winter transfer window open?

Once the summer deadline shuts, clubs will not be able to do any more business until the winter window opens.

In England, transfers will be possible again from January 1, 2027.

The window will run for a month, closing again on February 1 at 11pm.

Meanwhile, in the WSL, the winter window will open on January 4 and close exactly a month later on February 4.

And in Scotland, their window will open on January 5, closing at 5pm on February 4.

Sports.title: Gabby Agbonlahor speaks to Morgan Rogers about £117m transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor speaks to Morgan Rogers about £117m transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea

Gabby Agbonlahor has urged Aston Villa fans not to turn on Morgan Rogers as he nears a record-breaking move to Chelsea.

The 23-year-old is set to join the Blues in a £117million transfer to become the most expensive British player in history.



3 Rogers has agreed a six-year deal at Chelsea until 2032, with the option of a further 12 months Credit: Getty

Despite the Villans being set to play Champions League football in the 2026/27 season, with Chelsea not in Europe altogether, the England international has jumped at the chance to play under Xabi Alonso.

Versatile attacking midfielder Rogers departs Villa Park after two-and-a-half-years, where he scored 31 times in 125 games across all competitions.

One of those strikes came in last campaign's Europa League final against Freiburg - helping the club end their 30-year trophy drought.



He is one of three high-profile players that will depart the Midlands giants this window, with Youri Tielemans already joining Manchester United in a £35m switch.

Left-back Lucas Digne meanwhile is closing in on a return to Paris Saint-Germain after the Champions League holders activated his release clause - worth around £8.5million.



Roger that

After Arsenal refused to stump up more than £80m for Rogers, the player is now poised to be unveiled as a new Chelsea star.

For Villa cult hero Agbonlahor, he has revealed that he sent a text message to Rogers on Monday night after he passed his Blues medical.



Speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show, Agbonlahor said: "I watched him [at the World Cup], obviously, Aston Villa fan.

"And I had to message him last night, I said to him, 'Listen, thank you for everything you've done for my football club, wish you all the best in the future.'

He replied, 'Thank you, mate, I really appreciate it.'

3 Rogers proved influential in Villa finishing in fourth spot in the 2025/26 season

"And I want every Villa fan to be like that with Digne, with Tielemans, with Rogers.



"These players won our first [European] trophy since 1982 and have been a fantastic group of players for this football club.

"They've moved on now, no problem, I'm sure Morgan Rogers will get a good standing ovation when he comes back to Villa Park."

And Agbonlahor believes he will be a roaring success at Stamford Bridge - tipping him to reach another level under the tutelage of Alonso.

Commenting on where he could fit in at Chelsea, he remarked: "If Alonso does play that 3-4-2-1 that he liked at Leverkusen and play two 10s.



"He could play [Cole] Palmer and Rogers as two 10s, but he can play off the left - not off the right - it doesn't suit him over there.

3 Rogers scored three goals from 15 Europa League appearances in the previous campaign Credit: Getty

"But what you've got from this player is somebody who will receive the ball under pressure.

"And I've never seen a player who can drive with the ball- he's quicker when he's running with the ball.



"He's got such strength, skill and he can finish as well.

"Honestly you've got an all-round top player here in Morgan Rogers.

"I think he's going to get better and better.

"Let's not forget he's only 23, he's going to learn a lot from Alonso and I think he's going to be a huge success at Chelsea Football Club."

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes breaks silence on World Cup brawl as red card removed from record
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes has spoken out following Argentina's World Cup final defeat, which saw him at the heart of an ugly post-match brawl.

The midfielder was sent off after Spain's World Cup triumph descended into chaos at full-time, as members of the Argentina camp were involved in a series of bust-ups with their opponents.

4 Paredes had his red card for his post-match actions removed, despite repeatedly throwing Spain's Gavi to the ground Credit: Getty

Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner sealed victory for La Roja, and the 2022 champions lost all composure in the immediate aftermath.

Got away with one?

Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, as he threw punches and pushed some of the Spanish players in a furious scuffle.

Footage showed him grabbing Barcelona's Eric Garcia by the throat, before grappling with Gavi and throwing him to the ground.

This came after his Argentina teammate Nahuel Molina appeared to start the mass brawl by throwing a punch at Spain captain Rodri.

A series of altercations unfolded, with Paredes' actions the most violent, and it was reported at the time that he had been sent off by referee Slavko Vincic.

However, according to BBC Sport, the red card was later removed from the record and no disciplinary action was taken by FIFA.

Paredes could still be punished for his conduct, with FIFA set to launch an investigation into the ugly full-time scenes, despite getting an immediate reprieve.

'Chest full of pride'

In his first social media comments since Argentina's heartbreak, Paredes made no mention of his violent rampage as he awaits the outcome of FIFA's investigation.

He wrote on Instagram: "THANK YOU, ARGENTINA!!! I LOVE YOU, TODAY AND ALWAYS.

"Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves - but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again!

4 Paredes was at the centre as tempers boiled over at full-time in the World Cup final Credit: Getty

4 The Argentina midfielder soon turned on Spain's Gavi after he tried to intervene in the scuffle Credit: Getty

"Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team—to this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match!

"It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

Vow of silence?

Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card shortly before the end of normal time, giving his team a huge task as they looked to keep out a dominant Spain side.

But like Paredes, Fernandez did not acknowledge his costly actions, offering no apology and speaking only of his pride.

He said in a statement on Instagram: "As time goes by, you realise there is something much bigger than just a result."

"For years, this group has represented us in the best possible way. It teaches that competing isn't just about winning; it’s about giving your all for the jersey and never giving up."

4 Enzo Fernandez was shown a second yellow card in second-half stoppage-time Credit: Getty

'Disgraceful'

While Paredes opted not to mention his role in the violent post-match scuffle, the rest of the footballing world has weighed in.

The Argentina star has been widely condemned for his conduct, not least by talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who insisted Paredes should be banned from the whole of the next World Cup.

The Aston Villa icon said on the talkSPORT Breakfast show: "You want to feel safe on the pitch, the punishment has to be that big that no-one ever does that again.

"No matter what happens in football, you can be angry you lost, but be classy in defeat, if you want to fight Paredes, there are places to fight - not on the pitch against Garcia.

"And the way he was manhandling Gavi, a 21-year-old kid, and you were throwing him around on the pitch, that's someone's son, brother.

"Disgraceful. I would ban him from the whole next tournament if I had my way. Coward."

Historic precedent?

Paredes wouldn't be the first Argentine to be banned following a post-match brawl at a World Cup.

At the 2006 World Cup, after losing their quarter-final to Germany, Leandro Cufre was given a four-match ban and a £4,800 fine for kicking Per Mertesacker.

Maxi Rodriguez got a two-game ban for throwing punches and was fined £2,400, while Germany's Torsten Frings got a one-match suspension for his involvement too.

Sports.title: When is 2026 Community Shield? Season opener moved from Wembley for the first time in 20 years
Sports.content:
When is 2026 Community Shield? Season opener moved from Wembley for the first time in 20 years

The Community Shield marks the first fixture of the domestic season, and it will not be staged at Wembley Stadium for the first time in two decades.

Fans across the world will tune in to watch Premier League champions Arsenal take on FA Cup winners Manchester City.

3 Arsenal could be the team to beat again next season as they look to defend their crown in the Premier League Credit: Getty Images - Getty

The Gunners head into the match aiming to build on their title-winning campaign, while Enzo Maresca will manage his first game for City and kick-off their new era.

Why is it not at Wembley Stadium?

A major change of venue will see the clash move away from Wembley Stadium to an iconic ground that last hosted the event in 2006.

This is due to scheduling issues with pre-planned summer concerts taking place at the traditional venue.

The Weeknd is booked at England's national football stadium, performing his 'After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour with Playboi Carti'.

The official statement released by the FA confirmed supporters will have to cross the border into Wales for the clash.

They stated: "The 2026 FA Community Shield will be played at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday 16 August."

The event is historically held on the weekend before the league commences, which this season begins on August 22.

This meant organisers had to target mid-August, which unfortunately clashed with the concert dates.

The 74,500-capacity venue offers a strictly neutral ground for both competing clubs, ensuring that fans of both teams face a journey.

3 Palace won the Community Shield at Wembley last year Credit: Getty

The Welsh national stadium has hosted the Community Shield on six occasions between 2001 and 2006.

During that period, Arsenal played in four of the meetings, and won two.

Over the six years the fixture was relocated, only four teams competed across the border: Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, and Chelsea.

When is the Community Shield?

The 2026 FA Community Shield will take place on Sunday, August 16.

Kick-off for the match is scheduled for 3pm and will be held at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

The match will likely present supporters a first proper look at both teams before the Premier League season gets underway.

3 Maresca will take over from his former coaching sensei in Guardiola, and the fixture will mark his first as the Man City boss Credit: Getty

Who won the 2025 Community Shield?

Crystal Palace won last year's edition against Liverpool after securing their first-ever FA Cup.

The Eagles beat the Reds 3-2 on penalties at Wembley after playing out a 2-2 draw in normal time.

Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr scored for Palace in the draw, with Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong netting for Liverpool.

Marc Guehi lifted the trophy as captain under Oliver Glasner; however, he will be representing Man City on this year's occasion.

Similarly, Eberechi Eze also featured in a Palace shirt at Wembley last summer, but will be lining up for Arsenal instead.

Pep Guardiola and his side previously took home the trophy in 2024, 2019 and 2018.

Sports.title: When is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? Date, kick-off time and how to follow as PSG take on Aston Villa
Sports.content:
When is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? Date, kick-off time and how to follow as PSG take on Aston Villa

One of the opening games of the 2026/27 campaign is a clash between the two leading European champions next month.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain take on Europa League victors Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup.

3 PSG won their second consecutive Champions League, returning to the Super Cup Credit: Getty

PSG defeated Arsenal in the final of UEFA's elite competition, claiming the title for the second straight year by sinking the Gunners.

The French giants beat the Premier League champions on penalties following a 1-1 draw, as Gabriel sent his decisive spot-kick over.

They are also the reigning Super Cup winners after beating Tottenham in the game last term, so they are aiming to go back-to-back in this clash.

As for Aston Villa, they won the Europa League with a comfortable 3-0 win over German side Freiburg in Istanbul.

This will be Villa's first Super Cup appearance since 1983, having historically won their first European title in 44 years.

When is the 2026 UEFA Super Cup?

The 2026 UEFA Super Cup will be played on Wednesday, August 12.

Kick-off is set for 8pm UK time, which is 9pm local time.

It will be held at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria.

This is the first time a UEFA final has been played at this stadium, which is the home of Austrian giants Red Bull Salzburg.

The venue staged multiple games at EURO 2008 and will become the 14th ground to host the match since the competition switched from being hosted every year in Monaco 13 years ago.

3 Aston Villa are going to take on PSG after winning the Europa League last season Credit: Getty

UEFA Super Cup: How to follow

talkSPORT will have live coverage of the action from Austria.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

3 The UEFA Super Cup is played every year at a different venue Credit: Getty

Which club has won the most Super Cups?

The Champions League winners have won 30 of the 50 editions of the UEFA Super Cup, with PSG favourites for this one.

They can move to joint-fifth in the all-time list of Super Cup winners by claiming their second title in August.

Real Madrid have won it the most times with six successes, while AC Milan and Barcelona have lifted the trophy five times.

Liverpool are four-time winners, with Atletico Madrid three-time winners and Bayern Munich and Chelsea one of those on two.

As mentioned, PSG won the Super Cup last year, with Real claiming the title in 2024 and Manchester City winning it in 2023.

If Aston Villa come out on top in Salzburg, they will join Man City, Chelsea and Liverpool as the only English clubs to win the modern version of the UEFA fixture.

Sports.title: Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth contract as Premier League club see enquiry rejected
Sports.content:
Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth contract as Premier League club see enquiry rejected

Arsenal and Manchester United target Alex Scott has turned down the offer of a new contract at Bournemouth, talkSPORT understands.

Bournemouth's stance remains that they expect him to be their player next season even without signing a new deal.



2 Scott is a wanted man after a breakout season for Bournemouth Credit: Getty

The Cherries previously rebuffed an approach from Arsenal in June.

talkSPORT also understands Bournemouth rejected an enquiry from Chelsea for the midfielder.

Scott, who joined the Cherries from Bristol City in 2023, has two years to run on his current contract.

The 22-year-old's stock has considerably risen after he played a key role in helping Bournemouth finish sixth in the Premier League last term, which earned them qualification for the Europa League.



His performances prompted England manager Thomas Tuchel to extend an invitation to the Three Lions' pre-World Cup training camp in Florida.

Scott isn't the only Bournemouth star eyed up by the Premier League's big boys, with winger Eli Junior Kroupi also of interest.



However, similarly to their stance on Scott, the Cherries have informed rivals Kroupi is not for sale either.

Losing either Scott or Kroupi would be a major blow for new manager Marco Rose in his first season at the Vitality Stadium after he replaced Andoni Iraola, who exited at the end of his contract.



Who else is on Arsenal's radar?

With Bournemouth determined to hold on to Scott, Arsenal may shift their attention back to Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

talkSPORT understands the Gunners are expected to lodge another bid for the Magpies skipper having had a £55m offer rejected in June.

2 Guimaraes' future is set to be a hot topic this summer Credit: Getty

It is also understood Guimaraes has already agreed personal terms with Arsenal, meaning the two clubs now need to agree on a price for the deal to progress.



Arsenal have already swung big and missed in this transfer window, with Chelsea swooping in to sign Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers for £117m.

Rogers was the Gunners' top target but they were only prepared to fork out as much as £80m, opening the door for the Blues to complete a deal.

United has already taken steps to improve their midfield, landing Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa after they triggered his £35m release clause.

The Red Devils also signed Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50m.

United was desperate to revamp their midfield following the departure of Casemiro at the end of last season.

Sports.title: Arsenal to make improved Bruno Guimaraes bid as Gunners’ Morgan Rogers valuation is revealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal to make improved Bruno Guimaraes bid as Gunners’ Morgan Rogers valuation is revealed

Arsenal are set to test Newcastle's resolve yet again as they prepare an improved offer to sign Bruno Guimaraes, talkSPORT understands.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has identified the Magpies skipper as a priority signing this window as he looks to bolster his midfield.



3 Newcastle midfielder Guimaraes could be on his way out of St James' Park this summer Credit: Getty

talkSPORT first reported the Premier League champions' interest in the Brazilian last month.

The north London giants have already agreed personal terms with the 28-year-old, who has informed Newcastle of his desire to make the move to the Emirates.

Arsenal have seen an offer, via intermediaries, of £65million knocked back by Newcastle in their pursuit of the ex-Lyon star.



Gunner get ya?

But it is believed that they will soon return with a new offer as Arsenal look to finally get their man - years after being pipped to his signature by the Toon.

Prior to Guimaraes linking up at St James' Park in January 2022, last season's Champions League finalists had him on their radar, before Newcastle came in to swoop with a £35m deal.



Last week, we told you how Newcastle value their prized asset at around £100m.

Newcastle have been adamant that they do not intend to sell the player this summer, and are hopeful they can thrash out a new deal.



Guimaraes currently has two years left on his contract at Tyneside.

Arteta will be desperate to not miss out on another top target having been beaten in the race to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

The 23-year-old was Arsenal's number one priority, but pulled out of the running after refusing to meet the Villans' valuation.

3 Guimaraes' 2025/26 season proved to be his most fruitful in the Premier League to date

Chelsea, who had been keeping tabs on the former Middlesbrough man, came in to agree a whopping £117m deal with the Europa League holders.



And Arsenal were unwilling to match that fee, with the club only prepared to go as high as £80m to secure the services of the England international.

Rogers is now set to become the most expensive British player in history.

His £117m transfer eclipses the £116m Manchester City forked out to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest earlier this summer.

Who have Arsenal signed this summer?

Arsenal announced Piero Hincapie as their first signing of the window in June.

3 Arsenal deemed Rogers as too expensive - despite the player meeting Arteta for face-to-face talks Credit: Getty

And they then followed that up by snapping up goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer following his release at Leeds.

Greek winger Chrisos Tzolis is set to be their next arrival, with Arsenal agreeing a £34m with Club Brugge.



He will replace Leandro Trossard, with the Belgian leaving to join Turkish side Besiktas for £17m.

Arsenal remain in the market to bring in a new winger, with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola admired.

Meanwhile, versatile Atletico Madrid man Julian Alvarez is another option with the LaLiga club refusing to sell him to rivals Barcelona.

Sports.title: 'We still have the Falklands': Sister of Argentina thug who punched Spanish footballer at the World Cup final makes bizarre claim after nation's shameful behaviour
Sports.content:
'We still have the Falklands': Sister of Argentina thug who punched Spanish footballer at the World Cup final makes bizarre claim after nation's shameful behaviour

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The sister of Leandro Paredes shared a bizarre statement about Argentina's claim to the Falklands just hours after the national team lost their World Cup final to Spain on Sunday evening.

Disputes over the British Overseas Territory have been at the centre of Argentina's World Cup campaign, with the players singing anti-English songs throughout the tournament and displaying a banner parroting their claim to the archipelago after beating England in the semi-final.

But Barbara Paredes went one step further after landing in Buenos Aires following the team's defeat, claiming that she was consoled by the islands belonging to Argentina.

'We’re all delighted, but to be honest we didn’t expect to get this far, and having made it this far and come out on top against England – for us, that meant the world,' Barbara told reporters.

'We may not have the third or fourth star, but we’ve got the Falklands all to ourselves.'

Argentina have repeatedly attempted to assert a claim over the islands, which have been a British territory since 1833, and in 1982, launched an abortive invasion which led to the 10-week Falklands War.

" No ganamos la cuarta estrella pero tenemos las Malvinas para nosotros."



Hermana de Leandro Paredes, en Ezeiza. pic.twitter.com/ca8dgoCSth — Gabriel Alfie (@GabrielAlfie15) July 20, 2026

Leandro Paredes' sister Barbara had more incendiary comments on the Falklands after Argentina's World Cup final defeat

Paredes was heavily involved in the fighting which broke out after the loss in New York

Falkland Islanders most recently overwhelmingly pledged to remain British in 2013, with 99.8 per cent voting to stay British in an island-wide referendum.

But Argentina fans, players, and Argentine politicians whipped up what they believe is their own claim to the islands they refer to as Las Malvinas, with foreign minister Pablo Quirno suggesting that the referendum was illegitimate days before meeting England in last week's semi-final.

Quirno used an essay in La Nacion newspaper to claim the population had been 'artificially implanted by the occupying power', which was flatly rejected by Downing Street.

Meanwhile, Argentina lodged a diplomatic protest with the UK over what it called the 'unlawful' movement of a Royal Navy patrol ship near the South Atlantic archipelago.

In an official statement shared on X after the semi-final, the country's foreign affairs ministry expressed its 'strongest rejection' of the movements of HMS Medway and accused Britain of a 'military incursion' into its waters.

No 10 said the UK had notified Argentina in advance of undertaking a routine logistics visit and the British Navy 'always operates in full compliance with international law'.

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni had said before the game he did not want the fixture to become about the conflict over the territory.

But the country's vice-president Victoria Villarruel tweeted a victory message at full-time saying 'it wasn't just another match', alongside a video of what appeared to be Argentinian soldiers.

In the build-up to the fixture, she had described England as 'invaders' and 'usurping pirates'.

Premier League players Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez were among those who waved the banner after the final whistle on Wednesday, with more players in the team such as Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez set to return to England to resume their club careers after the summer break.

Despite urgent calls to FIFA to sanction players who breached the tournament's rules around the displaying of political banners, FIFA has not yet issued a sanction.

Argentina players were previously fined a paltry £20,000 in 2014 after displaying a similar banner, but European institution UEFA has since taken a harsher line, issuing one-match bans for Spain players Rodri and Alvaro Morata for leading chants of 'Gibraltar is Spanish' after winning Euro 2024.

The Boca Juniors star dragged Gavi to the floor after throttling Eric Garcia at full-time

Argentina are already under investigation after displaying a banner which supports their claim to the Falklands

Donald Trump's White House opted to back Argentina ahead of the final for using the banner, with the head of the FIFA task force Andrew Giuliani saying that it was allowed due to the country's First Amendment rights.

Argentinian president Javier Milei later waded into the row, declaring that his government was getting 'closer every day' to recovering sovereignty over the islands.

He wrote on X: 'While some are busy throwing tantrums befitting a terminally mononeuronal teenager, we, through the diplomatic route, are getting closer every day to the recovery of the Malvinas Islands, Georgias del Sur and the South Sandwich Islands, and the surrounding maritime space.'

But while Argentina may have felt free to display the banner again - after taking it to their team hotel last Wednesday - if they had won the final, the team did not get the opportunity to do so after losing to Spain 1-0 in extra time.

With the final whistle, and the loss of their World Cup title, Paredes was one of Argentina's players to mentally collapse, with the Boca Juniors midfielder disgracing himself with violent conduct.

Paredes throttled Eric Garcia in upsetting scenes before wrestling Barcelona star Gavi to the ground.

Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also involved in scraps, while Nicolas Otamendi tried to draw Player of the Tournament Rodri into an argument by accusing him of 'complaining to referees' in the build-up to Sunday's game.

With Paredes failing to be sent off after the final whistle, FIFA has since opened a second investigation into Argentina's conduct, appointing a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess the incident.

Sports.title: Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA
Sports.content:
Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA

Madeleine McCann's younger brother will represent Scotland in swimming at the upcoming Commonwealth Games.

Sean McCann, 21, has been selected to compete for the Scots in the pool at the home Games, with swimming beginning Friday.

Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three, back in 2007, and has been missing ever since. Sean was just two years old at the time.

19 years on, Sean is now making his senior international bow as a swimmer, and will compete alongside Olympic champion Duncan Scott for his national team.

McCann is a distance freestyler and is expected to compete in the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the slimmed-down Games.

His twin sister Amelie has also been selected by her country, but it is yet to be known whether parents Kate and Gerry McCann will attend the event to watch their children compete.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Shameless moment Argentina star fakes an injury in desperate attempt to save Enzo Fernandez from red card in World Cup final
Sports.content:
Shameless moment Argentina star fakes an injury in desperate attempt to save Enzo Fernandez from red card in World Cup final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Footage has emerged displaying Argentina's pathetic attempt to con the referee into reversing his decision to show Enzo Fernandez a red card in the World Cup final.

The Chelsea midfielder was given his marching orders in the 93rd minute on Sunday, after picking up a second yellow card for a recklessly late challenge on Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

Fernandez protested his innocence vehemently, but it was hard to argue against the decision of referee Slavko Vincic. Cubarsi had gone flying through the air after the foul.

And now a new angle of the foul has come to light, showing that Nicolas Tagliafico faked an injury within seconds of Fernandez flying in on Cubarsi, in an attempt to try and save the 25-year-old from being dismissed.

The full-back was walking normally until he spotted his team-mate's moment of madness, before dropping to the deck in an instant, holding his leg.

Lionel Messi then shamelessly rushed over to the referee after he had already gotten the red card out of his pocket, and pointed over to Tagliafico in a last-ditch attempt to prevent Argentina going down to 10 men ahead of extra-time.

The most shameless video of the World Cup Final



Enzo Fernandes kicks Cubarsi, an Argentina player fakes an injury and falls down, Enzo gets a red, Messi goes upto the ref pointing to Arg player down saying he’s injured review the foul 😭 pic.twitter.com/VLo00Oc32F — fan (@NoodleHairCR7) July 21, 2026

Argentina's Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card in the 93rd minute of the World Cup final

Nicolas Tagliafico (top left of the shot) could be seen faking an injury to try and distract the referee after Fernandez committed the foul

The desperate ploy failed to change Vincic's mind, and no amount of fakery could prevent Fernandez from being sent for an early bath.

Fernandez's dismissal rounded off an abysmal 90 minutes for the 2022 champions, who had no shots compared to Spain's 15.

Argentina went on to lose in extra time after Ferran Torres smashed home a 106th-minute winner to secure a second star on Spain's crest.

The ugly antics from the South American side worsened after the full-time whistle, with Leandro Paredes, who was incredibly lucky to avoid being sent off during the final, sparking a mass brawl during Spain's celebrations.

The midfielder was consumed by rage after the defeat and could be seen throttling Eric Garcia in the throat. Moments later, he pushed Gavi to the ground while thrashing his arms around.

Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved in the scuffle, too.

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

Fernandez sent Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air with his recklessly late foul

There were also ugly scenes after the full-time whistle as Leandro Paredes (centre) sparked a brawl

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart believed the post-match behaviour from Argentina was 'disgusting' while pointing out that Messi was the only player to show some 'class'. Meanwhile, Wayne Rooney wasn't surprised.

Rooney said: 'We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them. If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Sports.title: Unseen footage of Lionel Messi's bizarre World Cup final pep talk goes viral as he tells upset Argentina stars to 'relax and forget everything' moments before kick-off
Sports.content:
Argentina captain Lionel Messi gave a curious message to his players just moments before their World Cup final defeat by Spain, new footage has revealed.

Spain beat the 2022 world champions 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium on Sunday, triumphing thanks to Ferran Torres' goal in extra time after dominating the ball in one of the most one-sided World Cup finals ever staged.

Argentina, who had controversially edged past Cape Verde, Egypt and Switzerland before knocking England out in the semi-finals, were heavily criticised for their aggressive tackling and dirty tactics throughout the tournament - and their World Cup campaign ended in disgrace as they became embroiled in a mass brawl with Spain's players after the final whistle.

Speculation that something was not quite right within Argentina's camp has been circulating on social media after new footage of Messi addressing his players before the final was shared to social media on Monday.

In the video, as Messi prepares to lead Argentina out holding his country's pennant flag, he turns to his players who appear strangely downbeat and gloomy and says: 'Come on, guys, stay calm, folks. Let's stay calm, guys. Let's just think about playing, stay calm. Let's forget about everything. Let's just think about playing, folks.'

The curious message has led many fans to speculate whether Argentina's camp were in the right frame of mind heading into the huge match.

Wait... what the hell , look at this vid, Enzo was crying before the game and Licha looked like he'd been crying too.Then Messi says, "Let's forget about everything." What the hell happened before the 2026 World Cup final?????????pic.twitter.com/C3RUOrKKPB — Arvin (@sozirv) July 20, 2026

Lionel Messi delivered a curious message to his Argentina stars before the World Cup final

Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain ended with a disgraceful brawl on the pitch

Some supporters have theorised whether Messi was telling his team-mates to forget about world football's negative perception of them throughout the tournament, amid claims that World Cup referees had favoured Argentina in decisions throughout the knockout stage.

After staging a late comeback to win 3-2 against Egypt in the last 16, opposition manager Hossam Hassan furiously accused FIFA of rigging the World Cup after a string of controversial refereeing decisions went against his side.

Switzerland were also furious at officials after their 3-1 defeat by Argentina in the quarter-finals, as forward Breel Embolo was shown a controversial second yellow card following a VAR review.

Other supporters have suggested that Argentina's stars were emotional about the prospect of playing with 39-year-old all-time great Messi for the final time at the World Cup, despite him not having officially retired yet.

Argentina reacted disgracefully to Spain's celebrations at the full-time whistle as Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck and threw Gavi to the floor in shameful scenes.

Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Their emotional manager Lionel Scaloni then stormed out of his press conference in tears, saying: ‘We need time to reset and form another group like this one. It’ll be hard to recreate this one. It hurts my soul, I’m sorry.'

Responding to the video of Messi on social media, one fan posted: 'I know Spain are a quality team, but Argentina’s performance genuinely left me baffled. They looked nothing like the team we’ve come to know.

'There was no intensity, no urgency, no excitement completely different from the energy they showed in their previous games. Something felt off about that performance. I still can’t explain what I watched.'

A second fan said in a post: 'Argentina knew they couldn’t beat Spain so were trying to just make it to penalties.'

A third posted: 'Something weird is going on here. Very weird. Lionel's pep talk, Enzo's eyes, Licha's red nose… something VERY weird happened before the final.

'Neither Messi, nor De Paul, nor Paredes, nor Dibu, NO ONE is posting anything on social media. Minimally weird.'

Another conspiracy theorist added: 'At the Qatar final, they got off the bus totally unhinged, tearing through everything. Something happened, some argument with Scaloni, Tapia told them something, some FIFA sanction, I don't know.

'They were wrecked physically and mentally. I insist, something really shady went down there and we're gonna find out about it in 40 years.'

Messi was in tears at the end of the game and refused to watch Spain lift the World Cup trophy

Fans were not afraid to offer their speculative theories on social media in response to the video

Argentina also made headlines after the World Cup final defeat for refusing to watch Spain lift the trophy.

The defeated finalists collected their silver medals from FIFA supremo Gianni Infantino and US President Donald Trump on the stage at the MetLife Stadium but decided not to watch as Spain lifted the trophy - which is customary in finals of major tournaments.

Instead, the Argentina players, coaching team and staff walked over to the end where the majority of their fans were located and spent time gazing into the crowd with glossy eyes.
