Sports.title: Mike Tyson Crushes Carl Williams In 93 Seconds
Sports.content:
Williams had earned the opportunity the hard way. The 6-foot-4 challenger was the IBF’s #1 contender after victories over Trevor Berbick and other leading heavyweights. He had also gone the distance with former champion Larry Holmes, and his height, long reach and jab were considered his best weapons against Tyson’s relentless pressure.

Promoted by Don King and televised by HBO, the championship attracted approximately 11,000 fans to Convention Hall. Tyson reportedly earned about $5 million, while Williams received roughly $1.2 million. Ringside tickets sold for $500, although the event generated a much smaller gate than Tyson’s previous blockbuster title defenses.

Williams tried to establish his jab immediately while tying Tyson up whenever the champion closed the distance. Tyson continued stalking forward, slipping punches and waiting for an opening.

That opening arrived barely more than a minute into the fight. Williams fired another left jab, Tyson slipped outside it and answered with a crushing left hook that landed flush on the jaw. Williams crashed backward to the canvas. He beat referee Randy Neumann’s count but remained unsteady as he leaned against the ropes. After asking Williams if he was able to continue and receiving no convincing response, Neumann stopped the fight at 1:33 of the opening round.

The decision immediately drew boos from the Atlantic City crowd. Williams protested the stoppage, insisting he was able to continue, and his camp unsuccessfully sought a rematch. No second meeting ever took place.

The victory improved Tyson’s championship reign with one of the quickest heavyweight title fights in history. It also became the final successful defense of his undisputed championship before Buster Douglas ended his reign in Tokyo on February 11, 1990. Although the ending remains controversial, Tyson’s explosive left hook and the disputed stoppage have kept the fight among the most discussed moments of his championship career.

Sports.title: Roy Jones Jr. Says Errol Spence Takes Over Late Against Tim Tszyu
Sports.content:
Jones Jr. said Tszyu’s best opportunity comes in the opening rounds before Spence settles into his rhythm.

“Man, it’s a hard call, but I’m going with Errol. Hope Errol can withstand the early start that Tszyu is going to probably put up early because if you get past four or five rounds, Errol definitely is going to beat him because Errol, to me, is stronger later than anybody fighting. You get him past round six, and you got a problem in your hand. I don’t care who it is, especially if he ain’t beat up or nothing in the face. You get to round six, you got a problem because that’s when he starts to come alive. Ask Ugas. Ask Brook,” Jones Jr. said to Fight Hub TV.

Roy Jr. compared Spence’s relentless style to Marvin Hagler’s, arguing that constant pressure eventually wears opponents down. He also pointed out that Spence has more technical ability than many people remember from his amateur days, even though he has relied primarily on pressure as a professional.

The matchup remains a difficult one because Tszyu is naturally aggressive and has never been afraid to trade punches. That style may create entertaining early rounds, but it also plays into the kind of fight Spence has often thrived in if he can avoid taking too much punishment at the start.

Jones Jr. believes surviving the opening rounds is the key. If Errol reaches the middle rounds without absorbing significant damage, he expects the former unified welterweight champion to begin taking control with steady pressure and superior stamina.

A victory over Tszyu would put Spence back in the title picture at 154 pounds after a three-year absence from the ring. A loss would leave him facing another setback at a point in his career when every fight carries added significance.

Sports.title: Salvador Sanchez’s Final Triumph: The Classic Battle With Azumah Nelson
Sports.content:
The bout carried significant championship stakes. Sanchez defended both the WBC featherweight championship and The Ring featherweight championship for the 10th time. Already established as one of boxing’s premier pound-for-pound fighters, the Mexican star had built his reputation with victories over Hall of Famers Danny Lopez, Wilfredo Gomez, Juan LaPorte and Roberto Castanon.

Nelson came in as the WBC’s #10-ranked featherweight contender after accepting the fight as a late replacement. Largely unknown to American fans, the 24-year-old Ghanaian had never faced anyone close to Sanchez’s level, and most observers expected another successful title defense for the champion.

The unfamiliar challenger hurt attendance. Only 5,575 fans paid to attend the event, producing a modest gate of $129,244 despite Don King serving as promoter. Sanchez, as the champion and established attraction, earned the larger purse. Nelson also received the biggest payday of his young career, although the official purse figures were never publicly disclosed. Veteran referee Tony Perez worked the bout.

What unfolded surprised nearly everyone. Instead of being overwhelmed, Nelson attacked Sanchez from the opening bell with relentless pressure. He fired hooks, overhand rights and body punches, forcing the champion into one of the toughest fights of his title reign. Nelson captured several early rounds with his aggression and briefly had Sanchez backing toward the ropes, something rarely seen during the champion’s prime.

Sanchez began making the necessary adjustments. Beginning in the middle rounds, his timing became sharper. He started landing crisp counter left hooks, straight rights and punishing body shots that slowed Nelson’s relentless attack.

In the seventh round, Sanchez scored the fight’s lone knockdown with a sharp left hook, but Nelson beat the count and survived the remainder of the round.

Sanchez closed the fight by landing the sharper combinations and investing to the body, gradually breaking down Nelson’s offense before the 15th-round stoppage.

The conclusion arrived in the 15th and final round. Sanchez trapped Nelson along the ropes and unloaded a sustained barrage of hooks and body shots. Nelson remained upright but was no longer defending himself effectively. At 1:49 of Round 15, Perez stepped in and stopped the contest, awarding Sanchez a technical knockout after one of the finest performances of both men’s careers.

Following the fight, Sanchez praised Nelson’s toughness, later describing him as one of the strongest and most durable opponents he had faced. The fight proved career-defining for both men.

It became the final chapter of an extraordinary career for Salvador after his death on August 12, 1982, in a Porsche crash that deprived boxing of one of its brightest young champions. Many historians still rank him among the greatest featherweights in history despite his short career.

The defeat for Nelson became a launching point rather than a setback. The defeat raised Nelson’s profile, and he went on to win world titles in three weight classes before being inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

Over four decades later, Sanchez-Nelson has grown in stature. What appeared to be a routine title defense during the summer of 1982 is now remembered as one of the finest featherweight championship fights ever contested and the unforgettable final masterpiece of Salvador Sanchez’s career.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Taunts Keyshawn Davis After WBO Purse Bid Order
Sports.content:
“Anybody seen Keyshawn Davis?” Bill Haney posted on X.

The WBO’s order gives Devin Haney a commanding 75/25 purse split as champion if negotiations fail and the fight goes to a purse bid. Instead of celebrating a mandatory title shot, Team Davis suddenly finds itself staring at a brutal financial reality.

As champion, Haney is entitled to 75% of the winning purse bid and has little incentive to give ground while the mandatory process favors him.

The order also changes the conversation surrounding Haney’s options. Before the WBO stepped in, most of the attention was on a fight with Shakur Stevenson. Now the mandatory defense against Davis takes priority, and the July 27 purse bid deadline gives both sides limited time to reach an agreement.

If no deal is reached, the winning bidder will secure promotional rights for the fight under the WBO’s 75/25 split. That reality leaves Team Davis with an important decision. They can either reach terms before the deadline or allow the purse bid process to determine where and under what promoter the fight takes place.

Team Haney has little reason to blink before July 27. The WBO’s order already gives Devin Haney the financial advantage, leaving the pressure on Team Davis to decide its next move.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco Looks Much Improved Against Immanuwel Aleem
Sports.content:
Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn told the media at the post-fight presser that Pacheco made a sensible decision choosing to wait for a title match, being that he had a new training team and Pacheco preferred to take the fight until he was ready at 100 percent.

Saturday night, a much-improved Pacheco boxed a much more technically sound fight by controlling the distance, utilizing his jab, and being defensively disciplined. Against Sadjo, Pacheco took a lot of punishment and also suffered the first knockdown of his professional career, but against Immanuwel Aleem (22-5-3, 14 KOs), he showed another level.

He landed 44.2 percent of his total punches, keeping Aleem at range with his jab. Immanuwel struggled to get on the inside and was offensively ineffective, finding minimal success connecting on only 24.1 percent of his total punches (Compubox).

WBC interim world super middleweight champion Lester Martinez (20-0-1, 16 KOs) fought Aleem to a close and hard-fought 12-round unanimous decision. Many believed he would be a much more challenging opponent for Diego, but he proved otherwise.

After the fight, Pacheco expressed to the media at the post-fight presser his desire to continue his progression and fight the best super middleweights in the world. He’d like fights against Jaime Munguia, Christian Mbilli, Hamzah Sheeraz, and Canelo Alvarez.

It’s only his first fight under Buddy, and his potential is limitless. He demonstrated Saturday night at the War Grounds he has the potential to challenge for a world title. Hearn said he hopes to have Pacheco fight at this venue again this year, around October or November, but will keep their options open if a big fight comes along.

Sports.title: Olympic Gold And Professional Glory: Champions Who Conquered Both
Sports.content:
Among the earliest examples was Frankie Genaro, who won Olympic flyweight gold in 1920 before claiming the NBA flyweight championship as a professional. The 1924 Games produced three future professional champions in Jackie Fields, Willie Smith, and Fidel LaBarba.

The post-war era continued the trend with Pascual Perez, Floyd Patterson, Nino Benvenuti, Joe Frazier, and George Foreman. Patterson became the youngest heavyweight champion in history at the time, while Foreman and Frazier carried their Olympic success into Hall of Fame careers.

The 1970s and 1980s produced another remarkable generation. Michael Spinks, Sugar Ray Leonard, Pernell Whitaker, Lennox Lewis, Ray Mercer, Henry Maske, Mark Breland, Meldrick Taylor, Frank Tate, Patrizio Oliva, Maurizio Stecca, Mate Parlov, Leo Randolph, Giovanni Parisi, and Kennedy McKinney all captured professional world titles after winning Olympic gold.

Oscar De La Hoya extended that tradition after the 1992 Barcelona Games, becoming one of boxing’s biggest attractions while winning titles in six weight classes.

The modern era has added Guillermo Rigondeaux, Andre Ward, Yuriorkis Gamboa, Vasiliy Lomachenko, Robeisy Ramirez, and Robson Conceição to the list. Ward retired undefeated after becoming the unified light heavyweight champion, while Lomachenko captured world titles in three weight classes after winning Olympic gold in both 2008 and 2012.

Not every Olympic champion reaches the top of the professional game, making this list a reminder of how difficult it is to dominate both amateur and professional boxing. While Olympic gold opens doors, history shows that only a relatively small percentage of champions have gone on to win recognized world titles in the paid ranks.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Admits Discipline Failed Him Before Steven Butler Fight
Sports.content:
“I feel like I was just getting by just because of my talent,” Berlanga said on Brian Custer’s channel. “What separated me from those guys was my dedication and my discipline. I always gave myself 50%. This camp has been different. The light switch turned on.”

What Berlanga isn’t saying is that what played a part in him being able to get by at only 50% is how he was managed. The early narrative was built on a shiny marketing gimmick: 16 straight first-round knockouts. Top Rank arguably spoon-fed him opponents selected specifically to keep the streak alive.

Once he stepped up into actual eight- and ten-rounders against basic step-up opponents like Demond Nicholson, Marcelo Coceres, Steve Rolls, and Roamer Alexis Angulo, the knockout power suddenly vanished. He was getting dropped, biting opponents out of frustration, and looking completely ordinary against basic journeymen.

Matchroom essentially bought into the hype to leverage his Puerto Rican fanbase in New York, giving him soft touches like Jason Quigley and Padraig McCrory to line him up for a massive payday against Canelo Alvarez.

When Berlanga finally stepped up to elite level, the reality caught up with him. Canelo Alvarez outclassed him across 12 rounds, dropping him along the way. Hamzah Sheeraz exposed the gap in level by stopping him inside five rounds.

Attributing his struggles entirely to “lack of discipline” or “giving 50%” is a classic promotional spin to protect a fighter’s brand. Lack of dedication may play a role, but the primary reason he looked invincible early on was careful matchmaking hiding serious technical limitations, limitations that got punished the second he stepped in with elite competition.

“I want to change the perspective of people,” Berlanga said. “I want to be talked about like Bam Rodriguez, Shakur Stevenson… that I got skill, IQ. I owe it to myself.”

Comparing himself to operators like Crawford, Shakur, or Bam is completely disconnected from who he is in the ring.

Those guys are elite, generational defensive technicians and sweet scientists with master-level footwork, ring vision, and distance control. Berlanga is an aggressive brawler who relies on raw athleticism, wild power, and intimidating his opponents. You do not wake up at 29 years old after a decade of fighting as a crude slugger and suddenly develop elite IQ, nuanced defense, or counter-punching instincts just because you worked hard in one training camp.

It is one thing when a fighter is just spouting promotional buzzwords to hype a fight, but it is another thing entirely when they genuinely convince themselves of it. In boxing, that kind of delusion is dangerous.

Berlanga spent years being told he was an unstoppable monster while blasting out overmatched opponents in one round. That level of early praise distorts a fighter’s self-image.

Now, facing the reality of his technical limits, his brain is reaching for the easiest explanation: “I just wasn’t trying hard enough.” Accepting that you just lacked effort is a lot easier on the ego than accepting that you simply do not have the natural ring IQ, reflexes, or skill ceiling of a Crawford or a Shakur. If it was just a lack of discipline, it means the talent is still there waiting to be unlocked.

Sports.title: Lamont Roach Jr. Still Eyes Tank Davis Before Zepeda Fight
Sports.content:
“I’ve been moved on from a rematch with Davis, but if it presents itself, then obviously we’ll take it. You know, I really want to get what I deserve on paper. Even though I did it before, on paper I’d like that,” said Lamont Roach to DAZN.

Roach’s position is understandable. Many boxing fans felt he deserved the decision in his first fight with Tank, and a rematch would give him the chance to settle the issue officially.

Lamont followed that performance with another draw, leaving him without the type of win that would strengthen his position in negotiations for another marquee fight. Instead of rebuilding his leverage, he’s remained stuck while continuing to mention Tank and Shakur as preferred opponents.

Zepeda is one of the busiest pressure fighters in the lightweight division, and Roach will need one of the best performances of his career to beat him on August 1. A loss would leave him even farther from either Tank or Shakur.

Neither fight is close to becoming reality. Tank has other high-profile options available whenever he returns, and Shakur has repeatedly talked about Devin Haney and other major names since signing with Zuffa Boxing.

Roach may believe he already earned another opportunity against Tank, but boxing rarely works that way. Beating Zepeda is the only result that moves him closer to either fight. Another draw or a loss leaves him with even less leverage than he has now.

Ghana News.title: Ofori-Atta secures US immigration status after judge cites health, family ties and long stay
Ghana News.content:
Former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta has been granted an adjustment of status in the United States after an immigration judge ruled that his personal circumstances outweighed the concerns raised over criminal allegations filed against him in Ghana.

Judge David Gardey approved Mr Ofori-Atta’s application after considering his decades-long ties to the United States, including his education and professional career in the country, as well as his family connections.

The court noted that Mr Ofori-Atta had worked with major financial institutions in the US, including Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers, and also has a son who is a US citizen.

The judge also considered the former minister’s ongoing medical treatment, stating that his health had suffered following his detention over the criminal allegations.

“The court finds that the positive equities far outweigh the negative equities such that the court will exercise its discretion and grant the respondent's request for adjustment of status,” Judge Gardey said.

Addressing Mr Ofori-Atta directly, the judge said he had endured a difficult period but had been given the opportunity to present his case and had established that he was entitled to remain in the United States under the adjustment process.

Ghana News.title: US Immigration Judge says OSP allegations against Ofori-Atta lacked credible evidence
Ghana News.content:
A United States Immigration Judge has ruled that Ghana’s Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) failed to provide credible evidence linking former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta to any criminal wrongdoing.

Judge David Gardey, who presided over the case at the Annandale Immigration Court in Virginia, said the evidence presented by the OSP did not demonstrate that Mr Ofori-Atta had personally benefited from his role as a public official or engaged in any criminal conspiracy.

The ruling followed arguments by the United States Department of Homeland Security, which relied on criminal charges filed against the former minister in Ghana as grounds to oppose his application for adjustment of status in the US.

However, the court rejected the claims, describing the OSP’s affidavit as containing “conclusory allegations” without sufficient facts to establish criminal conduct.

“The court finds that the affidavit is lacking in any persuasive proof or evidence that the respondent has engaged in any criminal wrongdoing as alleged,” Judge Gardey stated.

The judge further noted that the absence of persuasive evidence of criminal wrongdoing was significant, adding that Mr Ofori-Atta had not been credibly shown to have committed any offence in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Samuel Sarfo joins Al Hala as Ghanaian defender targets another Gulf success
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian defender Samuel Sarfo has started a new chapter in his career after completing a move to Bahrain club Al Hala Football Club.

The experienced centre-back has signed a one-year contract with Al Hala, who are hoping his leadership and knowledge of Gulf football can help them achieve their ambition of returning to the Premier League.

Sarfo arrives at the club following a successful spell with Malkiya, where he played an important role in helping the team finish among the top four in the league and qualify for the Gulf Cup tournament.

The move represents another opportunity for the former Liberty Professionals captain to continue his long-standing career in the Middle East, a region where he has established himself through years of consistent performances.

The 34-year-old has previously played in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries, gaining significant experience in different football environments outside Ghana.

His latest move continues a career path that has seen him become one of Ghana’s experienced representatives in Gulf football.

Sarfo’s reputation for reliability and defensive discipline has made him a sought-after player in the region.

At Malkiya, he was part of a side that enjoyed a strong campaign, helping the club secure a place in the Gulf Cup competition while maintaining a competitive position in the domestic league.

Al Hala will now hope he can reproduce that level of performance as they pursue their objective of returning to Bahrain’s top flight.

Ghana News.title: Glasgow 2026: NPC Ghana deploys four accredited media officers at Commonwealth Games
Ghana News.content:
The National Paralympic Committee (NPC) Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to promoting disability inclusion by sponsoring four accredited Administrative Media Officers to provide comprehensive coverage of Team Ghana’s participation at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The officers, who depart for Scotland on Monday, 20 July 2026, are Michael Obeng, Administrative Media Officer for the Para Swimming Association; Bill Eshun, Administrative Media Officer for the Para Powerlifting Association; Prince Andrew Dornu Leiku and Theophilus Sampah, NPC Ghana Media-Level Administrative Officers.

Accredited by the Commonwealth Games organizers, the four officers will provide minute-by-minute reports, photographs, videos, interviews, feature stories and behind-the-scenes coverage of Ghana’s Paralympic contingent throughout the Games.

Beyond reporting, the assignment presents a unique opportunity for the officers to broaden their professional knowledge and practical experience in international sports journalism, media operations, digital storytelling and Paralympic communications.

The deployment marks another important milestone in NPC Ghana’s pioneering Media Administrative Officers Programme, launched in 2025 under the leadership of NPC Ghana and African Paralympic Committee President, Mr. Samson Deen.

The initiative saw the appointment of 38 journalists to various para sport federations and the NPC Ghana Communications Department as part of a national campaign to reposition para sports as a powerful tool for inclusion, empowerment, education and sporting excellence.

The programme was designed to increase public awareness, improve media coverage, educate journalists on disability sport and integrate communication professionals into Ghana’s broader para sport development agenda.

Representing Ghana at Glasgow 2026 are Zinabu Issah, Hayford Addai and Nkegbe Botsyo in Para Athletics, Promise “Wonder Atsu” Aheto in Para Swimming and Tahiru Haruna in Para Powerlifting.

The four officers will follow the athletes from their final training sessions through every stage of competition, documenting their preparations, performances, interviews, medal pursuits and inspirational stories for audiences back home.

Addressing the officers during pre-departure formalities, Mr. Samson Deen urged them to approach the assignment with discipline, professionalism and patriotism.

“You are not travelling to Glasgow simply to report results. You are going to tell the stories of courage, sacrifice and determination that define our athletes.

“Your work should inspire every Ghanaian to appreciate the value of inclusion and recognize the excellence of our Paralympians.”

“Remain focused, be prepared to sacrifice and continue inspiring our athletes to stay disciplined and target the podium. Glasgow 2026 is not only about medals; it is another important qualification pathway towards the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympic Games.

“Every performance, every lesson and every experience will contribute to Ghana’s preparations for LA28.”

Mr. Deen further noted that the responsibility of the media officers extends beyond publishing news reports.

According to him, their work should educate the public about para sports, promote disability inclusion and strengthen national support for athletes representing Ghana on the international stage.

Ghana News.title: Ghana, World Gold Council sign $250,000 deal to clean up artisanal mining sector
Ghana News.content:
Government and the World Gold Council (WGC) have signed a strategic partnership aimed at formalising artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), improving supply chain integrity and reducing illicit gold flows.

The agreement, signed through the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, seeks to establish a framework for responsible gold production by supporting policy development, capacity building, traceability systems, technology solutions and training for artisanal mining communities.

Under the partnership, the World Gold Council has committed an initial development grant of $250,000 to support efforts towards cooperative registration under Ghana’s flagship rCOMSDEP programme.

The initiative is expected to help create a national network of accessible and trusted gold processing plants that meet responsible sourcing standards while providing artisanal miners with incentives to channel their gold into the formal supply chain.

The partnership comes as Ghana continues efforts to address challenges within the artisanal mining sector, including illegal mining activities, environmental degradation and concerns over the transparency of gold trading.

The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah Kofi Buah, said the agreement demonstrates Ghana’s commitment to transforming artisanal and small-scale mining into a regulated and economically beneficial sector.

“This partnership reflects Ghana’s clear commitment to transforming artisanal and small-scale gold mining into a responsible, well-regulated and economically empowering sector.

"By working with the World Gold Council, we are strengthening our efforts to formalise ASGM, eliminate harmful practices, and ensure that the benefits of Ghana’s gold resources are realised by our communities and our nation as a whole.”

The Chief Executive Officer of the World Gold Council, David Tait, said Ghana’s position as a major gold producer makes the partnership important in building a responsible artisanal mining value chain.

“Ghana is a global leader in gold production and has demonstrated real ambition in tackling the challenges and opportunities of artisanal mining.

"This MoU provides a strong platform for collaboration — bringing together government leadership, international standards and industry expertise — to help build a trusted, transparent and responsible ASGM value chain that works for miners, communities and markets alike.”

The two parties say the partnership will focus on unlocking the social and economic benefits of responsible artisanal mining while protecting the environment and strengthening confidence in Ghana’s gold market.

Ghana News.title: Ghana defender Tariq Lamptey joins QPR after Fiorentina exit
Ghana News.content:
Ghana international Tariq Lamptey has joined English Championship side Queens Park Rangers (QPR) on a permanent transfer.

The move marks a return to England after an injury-disrupted spell in Italy with Fiorentina.

Lamptey and Fiorentina mutually agreed to end their relationship in May, bringing an early conclusion to a chapter in which he made only 25 minutes of competitive football appearances.

The defender suffered an ACL injury during his time in Italy but is now progressing in his recovery and is expected to return to selection in September.

“I'm excited for the opportunity ahead,” Lamptey said after completing the move.

“When I spoke to the gaffer and Christian (Nourry), the project was an encouraging one.

“The team have ambitious goals for this season, so I'm looking forward to it.”

Lamptey, who was born in Hillingdon and developed through Chelsea’s academy looks to rebuild his career and rediscover the form that once made him one of the most exciting young full-backs in English football.

The defender rose through Chelsea’s youth system before making his Premier League debut against Arsenal in 2019.

He later joined Brighton & Hove Albion in 2020, where he established himself as a key player and made more than 120 appearances for the Seagulls.

His performances on the south coast earned him international recognition with Ghana, and he represented the Black Stars at the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

Lamptey has since earned 11 senior caps for Ghana.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Argentina deny World Cup villains’ role after Samuel Jackson-led slants
World.content:
Hollywood actor Samuel L Jackson was among those who criticised Argentina at the World Cup, with racism among the allegations.

Critics blasted Argentina for dirty tactics and poor sportsmanship during their 1-0 loss to Spain, cementing the country’s status as FIFA World Cup villains, a reputation that grew throughout the tournament.

Allegations of racism against the South American nation’s fans, including from Hollywood actor Samuel L Jackson, were also rife.

Argentinians argue, however, that they are just passionate and misunderstood.

“I think we deserve some credit for not being very well-liked, because of this tendency to be arrogant and look down on most people from a pedestal,” said Leo Simone, 55, a lawyer, from his home north of Buenos Aires.

“They confuse arrogance with pride,” his wife chimed in, preferring not to give her name.

While star Lionel Messi is beloved around the world, anti-Argentina sentiment grew as critics argued they were FIFA’s darlings and received favourable referee calls such as penalties and cards shown to opponents.

Then came the final, replete with fouls, brawls on the pitch, and the Argentinian squad turning their backs when Spain received the World Cup trophy.

The New York Times called it a “tetchy, petulant and distasteful performance”.

Former Germany player Thomas Hitzlsperger wrote on X that Argentinians were “disgusting sportsmen” and British television personality Piers Morgan said “they basically just went around whacking as many Spanish players as they could”.

Near Ezeiza airport, where thousands of fans welcomed the players returning to Buenos Aires on Monday night, Maximiliano Heredia, a 35-year-old construction worker, said: “We’ve always been criticised, we’re used to it. But we always give it our all.”



Many Argentinians online wore the criticism as a badge of honour.

“There’s something about Argentine irreverence that they can’t tolerate. Our rebelliousness irritates them, enrages them … they call us cocky, cheaters, dirty. And we love it, it fills us with pride,” journalist Pedro Rosemblat wrote on his Instagram.

Sports journalist Ezequiel Fernandez Moores told the AFP news agency that some criticism was justified. “Sometimes we think we’re the centre of the universe, that God and our own navel are Argentine.”

He said local football codes of provocation, mockery and boasting did not translate to a global audience.

“We can’t expect the world to understand us, our way of being, feeling, and expressing ourselves,” he said.

Nevertheless, the team turning their backs on Spain as they received the cup was “not right”, he said.

Simone, the lawyer, rejected the notion that physical play makes Argentina a violent team.

“Argentina is a team that fights hard, like almost all South American football, but Spain also resorted to tactical fouls,” he said.

“It’s football: if you don’t like being hit, play volleyball.”

For Evelio Rubio, a 47-year-old Venezuelan neurologist who has lived in Argentina for a decade, it is impossible to understand from outside how “football is experienced here”.

For a Venezuelan accustomed to his national team not winning titles, experiencing that passion from within “is spectacular”.

Argentinian fans and some players have also faced accusations of racism, such as a chant sung by the team in the past mocking the Black players of France as not being really French.

There is also a long history of club-level fans throwing bananas on the field or making monkey gestures at Brazilian fans or Black players.

During this World Cup, FIFA condemned racism in a statement after an Argentinian supporter told a Black US influencer known as IShowSpeed to go “cry at the zoo” during a livestream.

American actor Samuel L Jackson stirred controversy when he urged Black people in an Instagram story not to support Argentina, which he dubbed one of “the most racist countries in the world”.

Sociologist Ivan Schuliaquer of the National University of San Martin said people should not take racism related to football and apply it generally to Argentinian society and history.

This racism exists and should not be denied, he said.

“But, in many cases, these labels come from colonising countries that have not yet fully resolved the issue of racism.”

World.title: Hormuz tankers on fire, as US, Iran continue attacks: What’s the latest?
World.content:
The White House told Al Jazeera that the US would continue strikes unless Trump decides otherwise.

The United States continued to attack Iran for a tenth consecutive night early on Tuesday, hitting military command centres. Explosions were reported in Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas and Bushehr.

Iran retaliated, striking US military assets in the Gulf, attacking Bahrain and Kuwait. Additionally, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said “massive fires” had also broken out on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Here is a recap of what happened on Monday night and Tuesday.

Where was Iran attacked?

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that it completed another round of strikes against Iran at 01:00 GMT on Tuesday. This marks the tenth consecutive night of US strikes against Iran.

CENTCOM said it hit Iranian military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites and air defence systems.

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Assidi reported from the Iranian capital Tehran on Tuesday that explosions were reported on Qeshm Island, the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as in the port cities of Bandar Abbas and Bandar Lengeh.

Explosions were heard in the southwestern city of Shiraz at about 1am local time (21:30 GMT) on Tuesday, Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster reported.

It said a location in the east of the city and another in the west “were attacked by the enemy”.

IRIB also cited the deputy governor of Isfahan province as saying there was no “enemy aggression or explosions” in the city of Isfahan or the wider province, denying an earlier report from the semi-official Mehr news agency.



The governor of Bushehr, meanwhile, told IRIB that the sounds of explosions in the province were “related to the activity of defence systems”.

The Mehr News Agency said on Tuesday that several explosions were in the city of Abdanan in Iran’s western Ilam province, citing Abdanan Governor Behzad Nourmohammadi.

Where was the Gulf attacked?

Bahrain: The IRGC said on Tuesday that it destroyed a US air defence system and radar in Bahrain’s Muharraq area during its latest military operation. In a statement carried by the IRIB broadcaster, the IRGC also claimed that a coordinated missile and drone attack destroyed a US Patriot air defence system in Bahrain’s Al-Riffa. The IRGC said the strikes were intended to clear the way for further operations. In a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, the IRGC claimed its aerospace force had destroyed Amazon’s central data infrastructure using cruise missiles.

Kuwait: The IRGC says it targeted and destroyed several US military assets in Kuwait during a recent strike. In a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, the IRGC said the strikes hit a long-range radar site, a telecommunications centre, satellite receiving systems and a missile defence radar of the US military in Kuwait. The group also claimed to have struck an MQ-9 drone hangar at the Ali Al Salem airbase, destroying or severely damaging several unmanned aircraft.

What have leaders of either side said?

Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett, reporting from Washington, DC, said the White House told Al Jazeera in a statement that the strikes would continue until the president decides otherwise. But it ended that statement by saying that diplomatic talks between the two nations are ongoing.

Iran’s IRGC said on Tuesday that “massive fires” had broken out on two oil tankers that attempted to “pass through the unsafe southern route in the Strait of Hormuz” following an explosion.

In a statement carried by the IRIB state broadcaster, the IRGC said rescue teams were evacuating the crews of the vessels.

It again warned shipping companies to safeguard the health of their crews, not to trust “false information from the US military”, and to avoid routes it described as dangerous.

“It is obvious that as long as America’s evils continue in the region, the Strait of Hormuz will be closed, and not even a drop of oil, gas, or a package of chemical fertiliser will be exported from the region,” it added.

World.title: Farage, Reform in ‘trouble’, as UK braces for crypto influence in politics
World.content:
Nigel Farage and his right-wing Reform UK party have been hit by a series of scandals following the disclosure of an undeclared personal gift of 5 million pounds ($6.7m) to the embattled politician by cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.

The gift, received before Farage became a member of parliament, is in addition to some 25 million pounds ($33.6m) in funding given directly to his party by Harborne. Amid growing controversy over the funding and his close association with convicted fraudster George Cottrell, Farage has made international headlines by resigning from Parliament and campaigning to regain his seat in a contest he has cast as himself versus “the establishment”.

However, all other leading parties in the United Kingdom have dismissed the move as a stunt and refused to put up candidates against him, leaving Farage’s principal political opponent for his Clacton seat as the satirical novelty candidate Count Binface.

Meanwhile, amid the whirl of memes and satirical commentary, both criminal and parliamentary investigations into the donations are continuing, with public scrutiny continuing to focus on Farage’s ties to Tether, Harborne’s “stable” cryptocurrency that has been widely linked to drug cartels, fraud and human trafficking — claims the company disputes.

Political and legal risk

“Farage and Reform are in a significant amount of trouble, and I think it’s only now beginning to dawn on them how much,” Sam Power, a leading expert in political financing, electoral regulation and corruption at the University of Bristol, told Al Jazeera.



Power said the Harborne donation scandal had hurt Reform in the Makerfield by-election, where their candidate lost to new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

“Politicians often assume that standards and ethics will never make the top 10 of voter concerns alongside healthcare and housing, but they do,” Power continued.

Reform, he said, currently held about 20 percent of the British vote solidly. That will not shift away. “But the remaining 10 percent they have — and will need to build upon to win an election — is already melting away,” Power said.

That Harborne would seek to back Farage and Reform was axiomatic, analysts have suggested.

Farage’s championing of cryptocurrency and opposition to government regulation of it are both longstanding and reflective of Farage’s right-wing allies in the administration of United States President Donald Trump, many of whom are tied closely to the world of cryptocurrency, estimated to be valued at somewhere between $2.2 trillion and $4 trillion worldwide, depending on market conditions.

Dangerous ground

“Crypto was born in the wake of the [2008] financial crisis as a way of separating payments — and essentially money — from banks and central banks,” economist Frances Coppola explained, describing early moves to privatise monetary control, freeing it from government — and in some cases democratic — oversight.

“The political underpinnings of crypto are essentially anarcho-capitalism,” Coppola continued. “It’s a rejection of the role of [centrally regulated] banks and central banks, and giving control over currencies to private companies,” she said.

That makes the “unregulated and fairly freewheeling world of crypto” intrinsically attractive to politicians on the far right and libertarian side of the political spectrum, Power said.

“It’s ideological as much as anything else: this idea that they’re all against the ‘establishment’,” he said. “There’s also the causal arrow of influence, where it’s not clear where the nexus of decision between the tech bros, Christopher Harborne, and Reform lies. It’s a mutually reciprocal relationship — at least, Harborne and others likely expect it to be.”

Murky waters

However, the lack of government involvement and difficulties in monitoring the use of the cryptocurrencies championed by Farage are having real-world impacts. As well as allowing for almost parallel economies in many developing countries, cryptocurrencies, including Tether, have become the currency of choice for organised crime.



While Tether, the company that launched the crypto, has stressed that it is actively working with authorities to combat the illicit use of its currency, the accusations against it are widespread. In Southeast Asia, specifically, the cryptocurrency has allegedly been used to abet human trafficking on an industrial scale and underpin scams and fraud operations worth millions. In 2024, a report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime concluded that Tether was the “preferred choice for crypto money launderers” in Southeast Asia.

“Crypto remains the currency for fraud,” said David Gerard, author of the Pivot to AI blog, who has written extensively on cryptocurrency. “If you look at human trafficking in places like Cambodia, it’s Tether that those carrying it out are relying upon.”

“Of course, when transgressions are reported, they react,” he said, reflecting the views of many who have highlighted Tether’s role in enabling global corruption networks, “but that’s often after the fact and too late”.

Farage has been documented using a September meeting with Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey to push back against the central bank’s plans to establish its own digital currency, which would have competed directly against Harborne’s Tether.

But the party denies any wrongdoing. Al Jazeera has also sought comments from Reform on other criticisms of Farage’s links to the crypto industry and Harborne, but has not received any response yet.

The Bank of England, meanwhile, has confirmed to Al Jazeera that no decision has yet been taken on whether to proceed with a digital pound, its proposed virtual currency.

To be sure, Farage has repeatedly denied being unduly influenced by Harborne, claiming that the 5 million pounds paid to him was a gift that he is free to spend entirely as he sees fit. However, while this last point remains the subject of a parliamentary investigation, others have sounded warnings over the potential influence of crypto on UK politics.

“I think we should be worried about politicians that are too close to crypto,” said Lucy Harley-McKeown, cofounder of Project Glitch, a blog examining emerging technologies. “I think we should be worried about who has control and influence over the democratic process. We should be concerned about the level of corruption adjacent to crypto and particularly what we’re seeing in the US,” she said.

Harley-McKeown was referring to Fairshake, a crypto-funded political action committee (PAC) powerful enough to swing elections that has funded pro-crypto politicians of all stripes across the country. Harley-McKeown also pointed to the case of the US president, who disclosed $1.4bn in personal income from crypto, including the sale of his Trump meme coin, in the 12 months leading up to June.

“This is the example Farage is looking towards,” Harley-McKeown said. “It’s not inconceivable that one day we could even be looking at a Farage Coin.”

World.title: Bangladesh face Australia Test might as Cummins, Hazlewood and Lyon return
World.content:
Australia return to full strength for two-Test series against Bangladesh, as injured trio return to strengthen squad.

Australia captain Pat Cummins, fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood and veteran spinner Nathan Lyon have returned from injury to be included in a ⁠13-man squad for next month’s two-Test home series against Bangladesh.

The trio were named on Tuesday for matches in Darwin (August 13-17) and Mackay (August 22-26), which form part of the World Test Championship cycle, after playing only three Tests between them ⁠during the Ashes in the last home summer.

Australia’s “big four” of Cummins, Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Lyon have not bowled together since the West Indies tour a year ago due to various injuries, but chief selector George Bailey said it was too early to confirm whether they would all turn out against Bangladesh, despite being fit.

“We won’t be locking in an 11 this far ‌out,” Bailey told reporters in a video call on Tuesday.

“We do know that across this two-Test series, the depth is there.”

With 295 Test wickets at an average of 24.21, 35-year-old Hazlewood has been one of Australia’s most devastating bowlers, but injuries have limited his output in recent years, including forcing him to miss the entire Ashes series with hamstring and Achilles problems.

In his absence, 37-year-old seamer Scott Boland took 20 wickets in an excellent series in the 4-1 defeat of England, and Bailey was frank about the competition Hazlewood faces from the Victoria quick.

“Scotty ⁠would never say it, but yeah, I think he’s mounting a strong case that ⁠when you use the words of big three (fast bowlers), that he could be one of those,” said Bailey.



Hazlewood’s recall means no place for Michael Neser despite the paceman’s fine Ashes campaign.

The squad is the first following opener Usman Khawaja’s retirement, potentially creating opportunity at the top of the ⁠order.

South Australia opener Jake Weatherald has been retained despite struggling during his debut Test series in the Ashes, when he averaged 22.33 across the five matches.

The pocket-sized left-hander has ⁠yet to convince, but Bailey said selectors saw positives in the opening combination ⁠with Travis Head during the Ashes.

“Hopefully we do see some growth out of that [Ashes] and some understanding of what it takes for success at Test level,” he said.

Cameron Green has also held onto his spot after a disappointing Ashes with bat and ball, and is one of two all-rounders ‌in the squad with Beau Webster.

Josh Inglis was retained as a potential middle-order batting option.

Australia sit top of the World Test Championship table midway through the cycle and will look to cement their place with a series win over ‌fourth-placed Bangladesh ahead of a tough tour of South Africa in October.

Australia squad: Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Jake Weatherald, Beau Webster.

World.title: Trump slaps 50% tariffs on Canada and Carney vows to 'intensify' trade talks
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on a wide range of goods imported from Canada, in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

Everyday consumer items like wine and hockey sticks and industrial goods such as cement are among the goods targeted. However, several key exports will be spared, such as energy, potash, critical minerals and fish.

Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by saying Canada stood ready to "intensify" trade talks with the US in the coming weeks.

The White House said the duties would take effect in 30 days. It marks a major escalation in trade tensions between the North American neighbours.

These tensions have been simmering since Trump returned to office in January 2025 and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs.

Tariffs are taxes on imported goods that are paid to the government by companies bringing in the foreign products.

The US Supreme Court ruled earlier this year that many of Trump's tariffs imposed globally under emergency powers were illegally enacted. But his latest action on Monday night uses a different, obscure law that is untested in court.

Canada, which is one of the US's closest trading partners, was one of the few countries to retaliate last year against Trump's tariffs.

It placed a 25% levy of its own on about C$30bn (Â£16bn; $21.7bn) worth of US goods being brought into Canada. Carney later dropped some of them.

A White House fact sheet published on Monday discussing the new tariffs said they applied regardless of whether the product was included under the existing free trade agreement between Canada, the US and Mexico, known as the USMCA.

The new tariffs add to trade barriers already in place between the two nations.

The US has been maintaining active tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on Canadian steel, aluminium and copper. It also charges a 35% tariff on Canadian softwood lumber, alongside a 25% tax on non-US parts in cars.

Meanwhile Canada has its own 25% counter-tariff on selected imports of American steel, aluminium and vehicles.

Monday's announcement also comes in the wake of President Trump's threat to impose tariffs over Canadian wildfire smoke drifting into US cities, though this issue has not been officially mentioned as the justification for the move.

World.title: US launches fresh strikes on Iran, as Trump warns of retaliation for deaths of soldiers
World.content:
The US military says it launched another round of strikes against Iran to "further degrade" its capabilities to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The strikes - the 10th consecutive night of attacks - come after US President Donald Trump vowed to punish Iran for the deaths of US soldiers.

In response, Iran said it struck two oil tankers in the waterway, as well as US military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, state news agency IRNA reported.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now fighting a "full-scale war" with the US. Trump earlier said Iran had been hit "very hard" the previous night "in honour" of three US soldiers killed recently - two in Jordan and one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest strikes had hit Iranian "military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems".

Explosions were reported near the north-western city of Tabriz, where state media said one person was killed and several wounded, as well at the Gulf ports of Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini and the south-eastern ports of Chabahar and Konarak.

Centcom also insisted that commercial vessels were continuing to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran meanwhile said its forces struck two oil tankers as they attempted to transit through what it called the strait's "unsafe and hazardous southern route" and rescue teams were picking up their crews, according to state media.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz had reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

It was not clear whether the tanker reported by UKMTO was among those cited by Iran.

Six fuel tankers and cargo ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to preliminary data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler. Two of these vessels had previously been sanctioned by the US for links with Iran.

This is down from eight vessels crossing on 19 July, the data shows. All but one of the crossings made on 20 July were via the northern route near Iran.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also claimed to have targeted a data centre belonging to the US company Amazon in Bahrain, according to state media on Tuesday.

The IRGC "attacked and destroyed the central data infrastructure of the American company Amazon in Bahrain with several cruise missiles," state news agency IRNA reported.

Jordan said on Tuesday that it had intercepted five drones after saying it had shot down three missiles late on Monday. Bahrain said drones launched by Iran had targeted its air navigation systems - but traffic remained unaffected. Kuwait's armed forces also said they had intercepted Iranian drones.

At the same time, Tehran said diplomatic messages were still being exchanged by both sides through intermediaries, despite a collapse of a ceasefire.

On Monday night the Department of Defense confirmed the identities of two of the US soldiers â Pte Isabella Gonzales, 19, from Texas, and Lt Tyler James Feehan, 25, from Hawaii - who were killed in an Iranian strike on the Muwaffaq Salti base in Jordan over the weekend.

Centcom said earlier a third service member also went missing in action after the attack, and unidentified remains were later found in the area.

World.title: Lebanese army says troops deploying in 'pilot zone' after Israeli withdrawal
World.content:
Lebanon's army says its troops have begun deploying to a "pilot zone" in the south of the country following the withdrawal of Israeli forces under a US-brokered agreement reached last month.

A statement from the army command said units had entered the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh in Nabatieh district on Tuesday morning.

On Monday night, Israel's military confirmed the start of the pilot zone plan, which should see Israeli troops pulling out of a small part of the territory occupied during their conflict with Hezbollah as well as the disarmament of the Iran-backed group.

It comes ahead of a meeting in Washington between US President Donald Trump and his Lebanese counterpart, Joseph Aoun.

Aoun is expected to urge Trump to put pressure on Israel to withdraw from the rest of southern Lebanon and to provide support to the Lebanese army to take full control of areas where Hezbollah holds sway.

Lebanon was drawn into the war between Israel, the US and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

Israel responded by launching a bombing campaign across Lebanon and invading a significant part of the country's south.

More than 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon, including almost 800 children, women and medics, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

Israeli authorities say 37 Israeli soldiers and four civilians have been killed on both sides of the border during the conflict.

World.title: Yemen's Houthis announce 'maritime embargo' on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The Red Sea has become crucial for oil shipments from Saudi Arabia during the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

It comes a week after the most significant escalation in the largely dormant conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia since an informal truce took effect in 2022.

The Houthis said they had launched missiles at Abha airport in south-western Saudi Arabia in response to air strikes on Sanaa's airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The strikes were claimed by the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, which said it had wanted to prevent an Iranian plane from landing in the capital without authorisation.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.

On Monday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi Arabia had imposed an "unjust and oppressive siege on our dear people for nearly 12 years, plundering our resources and imposing a comprehensive blockade on our ports and airports by land, sea, and air".

He then announced that the group had decided to respond by declaring a "maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of 'an eye for an eye'".

"Any foolish act committed by the reckless Saudi enemy through all escalation will be met with a comprehensive and decisive escalation," he added.

Sarea did not provide any further information about the embargo, but the deputy head of the Houthi media office, Nasruddin Amer, wrote on X that the group's forces were "closing Bab al-Mandab to Saudi enemy ships".

World.title: 'Anti-ICE' army veteran started fire outside Manhattan federal building, say officials
World.content:
A former US Army soldier has been arrested after igniting a fire in front of a federal building in New York City, says the FBI.

Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly shot a pellet gun and set off fireworks on Monday morning at 26 Federal Plaza, where the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and US Citizenship and Immigration Services have offices.

Federal agents tackled the suspect, who they say was armed with a machete and other weapons.

Three people sustained minor injuries in the incident, including an immigrant who was attending a status hearing, said the FBI. The lower Manhattan site has become a flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

The suspect, whom the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) called an "anti-ICE rioter", launched fireworks before pouring an accelerant on the stairs of an entrance to the building, causing a fire. The BBC has contacted DHS for comment.

The fire department put out the blaze.

Arrabaca "made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident", the FBI said.

FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle said during a news conference that Arrabaca was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks.

He fired about five to seven pellets from an airsoft gun in the direction of the building, Barnacle said.

Of those injured, two were government employees, Barnacle said.

DHS said a bystander was grazed, and a security officer who tackled and detained Arrabaca sustained minor injuries.

"He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist," Barnacle added.

Arrabaca, of Poughkeepsie, New York state, served in the regular Army from 2001-04 and in the Army National Guard-New York from 2004-05, according to the BBC's US partner CBS.

He did not have any deployments and left the Army with the rank of specialist.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the incident "deeply disturbing" in a post on X.

"Our administration will continue to ensure that every New Yorker is safe in their city - and hold accountable any who threaten that," he said.

World.title: At least 27 dead and 83 missing after passenger ferry capsizes off Guyana
World.content:
At least 27 people have drowned after a passenger ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana on Saturday night local time.

Sixty-nine people aboard the MV Barima had been rescued, Prime Minister Mark Phillips told reporters on Monday, adding 83 more remained missing.

Divers continue to search the site where the vessel capsized and people who believe their loved ones may have been on board the stricken vessel have been asked to contact the authorities.

"Our focus again is on finding people," said Phillips. "We still have hope."

An investigation into the tragedy had been launched, he said earlier.

"Let me be absolutely clear: where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law," he said.

Guyana's Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, expressed his anger at a news conference on Sunday, accusing those who operated the ferry of trying to "cheat the system".

The official registry had listed 133 as being on board the ferry, but Phillips said on Monday he was now "confident" there were 179 people.

Edghill also said the ferry's captain and at least one crew member had tested positive for cannabis.

"We have zero tolerance for members of the crew drinking or smoking while at work. And for us to have positive tests from the captain... this is serious," the minister said.

He added the captain and several of his crew had been taken into police custody.

World.title: Tate brothers appear in US court for extradition proceedings
World.content:
