World.title: Iranian forces target Bahrain and Kuwait after US hits Iran’s south
World.content:
IRAN TARGET. Military equipment targeted at an unknown location, during what US Central Command (CENTCOM) says are strikes on Iran, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on July 20, 2026.

Despite the escalating cycle of attacks that has all but wrecked an interim peace agreement signed in June, signs that Tehran and Washington want to resume diplomacy keep oil prices in check

DUBAI, UAE – US forces bombed targets in southern Iran overnight after President Donald Trump said Tehran would pay dearly for the deaths of American soldiers, while Iran targeted US sites in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan and a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

The exchanges came a day after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said they would impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, opening a potential new front in the war and raising the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf.

Despite the escalating cycle of attacks that has all but wrecked an interim peace agreement signed last month, signs that Tehran and Washington want to resume diplomacy kept oil prices in check.

US Central Command said it had completed its latest round of strikes on Iran, saying it hit Iranian military command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems.

Explosions were heard around the city of Shiraz in southern Iran, while Konarak and Chabahar on the southern coast also came under attack, according to state media.

Iran responded with renewed attacks across the Gulf, where recent strikes on desalination facilities have raised concerns about water shortages and underscored the growing threat to civilian infrastructure.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted infrastructure in Bahrain belonging to US tech company Amazon in retaliation for what they described as a US strike on the construction site of Iran’s planned Darkhovin nuclear power plant.

Iranian state media reported that Iranian forces also targeted accommodation facilities used by US military personnel at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa Air Base. There was no immediate comment from the US military, Bahrain or Amazon on the reported incidents, which Reuters was unable to verify.

The Iranian army said it launched drone attacks against three US military bases in Kuwait on Tuesday. The Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a US military site in Jordan, and Jordan said its forces intercepted and destroyed five Iranian drones.

Tankers struck

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Tuesday a tanker in the strait reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

Also on Tuesday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers had caught fire after explosions while attempting to transit the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz. It was not immediately clear when those incidents took place.

Iran had been pressing the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the US continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure — putting two of the world’s most vital energy arteries at risk.

A full closure of Bab el-Mandeb would reduce global oil supply by 7% as it would leave most Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the huge cut to oil flows from the war in the Gulf, which has already reduced shipments by 10% of global supply.

After the Houthis announced their blockade, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it began implementing protection measures for its ships moving through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Oil markets weighed the threat to shipping against reports of diplomatic efforts to contain the conflict, with benchmark Brent crude prices easing slightly in early trading.

Diplomatic push to restore ceasefire

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday that Tehran had received a proposal from mediators for a 10-day ceasefire in efforts to salvage the interim deal, intended to pave the way to a lasting agreement to end the war that began on February 28 with US-Israeli attacks on Iran.

Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni had asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in the conflict. He later arrived in Islamabad for further talks.

The latest phase of fighting has proved to be among the deadliest of the conflict for US forces. US troop deaths rose to 17 over the weekend.

Trump, under mounting pressure at home over rising gasoline prices since the war began, said the latest US strikes on Iran were honoring the deaths of American service members.

“Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over! This directive has been passed on to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine, and every Leader in the Military,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday.

The war has killed thousands of people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. Parts of Lebanon remain under Israeli occupation following attacks on Israel by Hezbollah fighters, who said they were acting in solidarity with Tehran.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun is due to meet Trump at the White House on Tuesday to present a plan on how to disarm Iran-aligned Hezbollah and secure an Israeli withdrawal. – Rappler.com

World.title: US, China to hold AI talks in September – sources
World.content:
The AI talks, a significant outcome of the Trump-Xi summit in May, will likely take place before Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned September 24 visit to the US, although the dates have not been finalized, sources say

BEIJING, China – The United States and China are planning to hold talks over AI in September, five sources familiar with the matter told Reuters, as the superpowers confront how to regulate the risks posed by their increasingly powerful rival frontier models.

The AI talks, a significant outcome of the Trump-Xi summit in May, will likely take place before Chinese President Xi Jinping’s planned September 24 visit to the US, although the dates have not been finalized, said the sources, who asked not to be named as the information is not public.

The talks would be led on the US side by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, four of the sources said. The identity of other participants on the US and Chinese side, as well as the agenda and location of the discussion, are still under deliberation as preparations are at an initial stage, three of them said.

The White House, US State Department and US Treasury did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. China’s National Development and Reform Commission, cyberspace regulator, industry and foreign ministries, and the State Council did not immediately respond to faxed requests for comment. – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: Romualdez did not ‘dare’ Senate to investigate him; video is AI-generated
World.content:
While the former House speaker has denied allegations that he masterminded a corruption scheme in the government, he did not make the statements shown in the video

Claim: In a video, former House speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez denied being the central figure in corruption scandals in the government and challenged the Senate to invite him to its probe.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: The video was posted by a Facebook page named PolPolitika on July 15. As of writing, the video has garnered more than 2,100 reactions, 1,700 shares, and 700 comments.

The video appears to show Romualdez being interviewed onboard a ship, where he says, “Sa mga Pilipinong hindi bumibitaw, hindi niyo ba naisip? Imposible talaga na ako ang nag-approve ng budget. Common sense na lang talaga.”

(To the Filipinos who aren’t letting this issue go, haven’t you thought about it? It’s impossible that I approved the budget. It’s just common sense.)

“Bakit ako palagi ang puno’t dulo ng lahat ng ito? Imbitahan nila ako sa Senado. Hindi ako natatakot kahit kanino,” he added.

(Why am I always the one tagged as the central figure in all of this? Invite me to the Senate. I’m not afraid of anyone.)

Romualdez also allegedly calls out Senators Vicente Sotto III, Panfilo Lacson, and the Tulfo brothers while challenging the upper chamber to invite him to their hearings on alleged corruption in flood control projects.

Many social media users believed the post, with some urging the former House speaker to appear before the Senate while others called on Romualdez to drop the names of those involved in the system of corruption.

The facts: The video is AI-generated. Results from the AI video detection tool detectvideo.ai showed a 64% likelihood of use of AI generation tools with high confidence level. Humantext.pro also flagged it as AI-generated with a rating of 72%.

There are no reports from credible media outlets citing Romualdez as making the statements shown in the video.

‘Central figure’ in corruption scandal: Romualdez has been implicated in corruption allegations, particularly the flood control ghost projects and budget insertion scheme.

In November 2025, former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co released a video accusing Romualdez and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. of being the masterminds behind insertions in the 2025 national budget.

The Office of the Ombudsman also tagged the Leyte representative as a “central figure” in the flood control corruption scandal.

“Our investigation identifies former speaker Romualdez as the central figure in a scheme built on the diversion of public funds meant for flood control projects — funds that were supposed to shield Filipino communities from the very floods that, year after year, take their homes, their livelihoods, and too often, their lives,” Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said on Monday, July 20.

The former House speaker, however, has repeatedly asserted his innocence. While he did not attend Senate hearings on the budget corruption controversy, he has denied the allegations against him and insisted that he won’t allow himself to be a “fall guy.” (WATCH: Breaking down Romualdez’s response to corruption claims)

Romualdez is currently placed under a precautionary hold departure order along with other individuals allegedly involved in the corruption scandal. The US government also canceled Romualdez’s diplomatic and tourist/business visas.

Earlier this year, the Court of Appeals ordered the freezing of assets linked to Romualdez. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: Landbank, Visa launch government credit card with spending controls
World.content:
CREDIT CARD. Visa Philippines country manager Jeffrey Navarro (4th from left), Landbank executive vice president Marilou Villafranca (5th from right), and first vice president Kristine Marie Cuevas (4th from right) pose with other representatives of various government agencies.

Landbank's government credit card also comes with an expense management system that captures transactions, matches expenses with receipts, and facilitates approval processes

MANILA, Philippines – Land Bank of the Philippines (Landbank) and Visa have launched a customizable government credit card, which they assert will give agencies tighter control over public funds and provide a better audit trail.

The Landbank Visa Government Purchase Card (GPC) works much like a corporate credit card issued to agency heads and authorized officers. Agencies can set a credit limit for each cardholder and restrict transactions to approved merchant categories, such as travel, fuel, representation expenses, and low-value purchases.

Landbank executive vice president and branch banking group head Marilou Villafranca said the card would reduce the need for employees to request cash advances, spend their own money, and later submit documents for reimbursement or liquidation.

“This will cut the manual processes or paper-based cash advances as well as liquidation,” Villafranca said. “Because it works like a credit card, you just use your card and then, upon the billing cycle, the agency will have to pay the entire amount.”

Expense management system for government

Purchase cards have long been offered to companies, but Visa Philippines country manager Jeffrey Navarro said the main differentiator in the Landbank program is its accompanying expense management system.

The platform will automatically capture transactions, match expenses with receipts, facilitate approval processes, and generate reports showing how much was spent, by whom, and under which department or spending category.

Transactions outside an employee’s approved limit or spending rules may be rejected or flagged for further approval.

“By providing accurate data, it can allow more financial control and better governance by the implementing institution,” Navarro said. “It’s not just a card na all of a sudden you can just spend digitally.”

The platform is scheduled to become fully operational by the fourth quarter of 2026.

Villafranca said the system could also be made accessible to the Commission on Audit, allowing state auditors to view spending information using the same data available to the agency.

“From the time you use your card, that’s already transparent in the expense management system,” she said.

The Bureau of the Treasury is among the first government institutions to adopt the Visa-backed program, which has an expense management system component.

Landbank clarified that its wider government purchase card program had already onboarded 107 agencies since 2023. Around 773 cards have so far been issued, mostly to agency heads and senior officers.

What is new in the latest rollout is the Visa expense-management system, which 17 government offices are initially set to use.

The bank eventually wants to expand the program beyond national government agencies to state universities, government corporations, local governments, and possibly barangays. – Rappler.com

World.title: Marcos summons Beijing envoy as PH-China tensions rise
World.content:
PH-CHINA TIES. President Marcos summons Chinese ambassador Jing Quan 'over maritime incident at Ayungin Shoal,' says Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro. Marcos was joined in the meeting by the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA)'s Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim and Assistance Secretary Marshall Louis Alferez. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto was also in the meeting.

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has summoned Chinese Ambassador to Manila Jing Quan late Tuesday, July 21, a day after a Filipino soldier was injured in a violent confrontation with China Coast Guard (CCG) personnel in Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal in the West Philippine Sea.

The July 21 meeting would be the first time for Marcos to summon Jing, who arrived in Manila in December 2025. Marcos had summoned Jing’s predecessor, Huang Xilian, twice: over the CCG’s use of lasers on the Philippine Coast Guard in 2023, and after Beijing announced sanctions on former senator Francis Tolentino, who is now Marcos’ labor chief.

A year after Tolentino was sanctioned, Beijing then sanctioned Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. That means two of Marcos’ Cabinet members are sanctioned by Beijing.

The development comes as tensions between the Philippines and China — in both political and maritime spaces — turn extra tense, and as Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visits Manila for the first time since July 2022 or the early months of the Marcos presidency. Wang is here for high-level Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meetings.

A racist video released by state-owned China Daily depicts the Philippines as a monkey to undermine the landmark 2016 Arbitral Award has sparked outrage among Filipinos.

On Monday, July 20, a Filipino soldier stationed at the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal sustained a gash after the CCG hit him on the head with a “wooden baton” during a melee between the two sides.

The CCG vessel, which anchored close to the BRP Sierra Madre, deployed a rigid hull inflatable boat with eight of its personnel on board the morning of the 20th. According to the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), the CCG boat then went around the Sierra Madre while taking photos and videos. The Philippines deployed two rubber boats with two and five soldiers on board to shoo away the CCG.

Chaos broke out when the CCG refused to leave. Beijing has accused Manila of instigating the confrontation and “deliberate provocation” during what it said was a “routine patrol” in Ayungin Shoal, which China calls Ren’ai Jiao.

PH-CHINA TIES. President Marcos summons Chinese ambassador Jing Quan ‘over maritime incident at Ayungin Shoal,’ says Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro.

Reset in China ties?

The BRP Sierra Madre is a World War II vessel that was ran ground in Ayungin Shoal in 1999, in response to China’s building activities in Mischief Reef, a feature close by. Beijing had claimed back in 1995 that the structure was merely a fisherman’s shelter. It is now a militarized artificial island.

Beijing claims Ayungin Shoal as their territory, even if it’s a low-tide elevation that generates no territorial claim or territorial waters. It is just over 100 nautical miles from Palawan, which means Ayungin is right within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, an area affirmed by the landmark 2016 Arbitral Award which China does not recognize.

Marcos, in early 2026, signaled a desire to reset ties with China after years of tense ties, mostly over maritime issues. China claims almost all of the South China Sea, including parts that are claimed by the Philippines and part of its exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

China’s insistence on its supposed historical claims have meant, for Filipinos, the danger of harassment out at sea. Chinese maritime units, typically its CCG, have used dangerous maneuvers, ramming, and water cannons to drive away Philippine vessels during their missions to the West Philippine Sea.

Harassment can extend to Filipino fisherfolk with much smaller wooden vessels.

Ayungin had become relatively peaceful since Manila and Beijing agreed on a provisional arrangement covering resupply missions to the BRP Sierra Madre. It’s unclear if the arrangement still stands after the latest clash.

US, Australia condemn Chinese actions

In a statement early Tuesday, July 21 (July 20 in Washington DC), the United States State Department condemned China’s “dangerous and aggressive actions” in the shoal and called on Beijing to “immediately cease its destabilizing conduct.

“China’s troubling pattern of provocation against lawful Philippine maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability and directly contradicts China’s repeated commitments to resolve disputes peacefully,” said State Department Deputy Spokesperson Tommy Pigott.

“We reaffirm the July 2016 Arbitral Tribunal ruling, which found that China’s expansive maritime claims in the South China Sea have no basis in international law. That decision is final and legally binding on both China and the Philippines. We will continue to stand with our Allies and partners in defense of a free and open Indo-Pacific,” said Pigott.

UN State Secretary Marcos Rubio arrived in Manila early Tuesday for the high-level ASEAN meetings.

The US is the Philippines’ only treaty-ally. The two countries are bound by the Mutual Defense Treaty, which covers areas in the South China Sea.

Australian Ambassador to Manila Marc Innes-Brown, meanwhile, said in a post on social media that Canberra “remains concerned about destabilising and dangerous conduct in the South China Sea, including actions by Chinese vessels toward Philippine vessels yesterday.”

“We continue to call for adherence to UNCLOS,” said Innes-Brown. The Philippines and Australia are strategic partners and have a Status of the Visiting Forces Agreement in place, allowing training between its militaries.

In social media posts, Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya said Tokyo was “seriously concerned about the aggressive actions in Second Thomas Shoal which resulted in injury to PH personnel and damage to the [Philippine] boat.”

He added: “We stand with countries in maintaining and enhancing the free and open international order based on the rule of law. The Philippines and Japan are Comprehensive Strategic Partners and have a Reciprocal Access Agreement in place akin to the SOVFA. – Rappler.com

World.title: Sara Duterte trial: Matibag says no hitman yet, but NBI has persons of interest
World.content:
WITNESS. National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag takes an oath before testifying in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026.

The prosecution, through the NBI director, brings up Duterte's assault of a sheriff, and her alleged role in the EJKs in Davao City, to establish her pattern of violence

MANILA, Philippines – National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag said the agency is still in the process of investigating the identity of the alleged hitman whom Vice President Sara Duterte hired to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Taking the witness stand of the impeachment court on Tuesday, July 21, Matibag said the NBI has “persons of interest” who can help lead them to the actual assassin whom the Vice President allegedly spoke with.

Duterte first said during her infamous virtual press conference on November 23, 2024, that she had reached out to an assassin to kill Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez, if something bad were to happen to her.

“I cannot disclose the identity of our persons of interest because… this is a continuing and open investigation,” Matibag said. “Our investigation will be compromised, and it will endanger our informants on the ground who can provide human intel.”

Play Video

Lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro conducted the direct examination of Matibag, who said that the agency is treating Duterte’s statement not as a threat, but as a “plan” to kill the chief executive.

The prosecution’s line of questioning led Matibag to link Duterte’s November 2024 statement, with two other statements related to an implied beheading of the President:

On October 18, 2024, Duterte said she had fantasies to decapitate the President.

On April 12, 2026, Duterte’s brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, told a political gathering of the RAGE Coalition that it wanted Marcos’ head.

The prosecution also played the video of Duterte punching a sheriff when she was Davao City mayor in 2011, and let Matibag read an affidavit of self-confessed Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas that implicated the Vice President in the extrajudicial killings in Davao City.

The pieces of evidence are meant to establish Duterte’s pattern of violence. – Rappler.com

World.title: Funds, resources for learners with disabilities still not enough despite 2022 law
World.content:
SCHOOL OPENING. Students attend the first day of classes at Legarda Elementary School in Manila on August 29, 2023.

A House committee finds that inclusive education is not yet a reality for many learners with disabilities

MANILA, Philippines – Lawmakers questioned the pace of implementation of Republic Act No. 11650, a law mandating inclusive education for learners with disabilities (LWDs), four years after the measure’s passage in 2022.

During a Department of Education (DepEd) briefing before the House basic education committee on Monday, July 20, Pasig City Representative Roman Romulo flagged the lack of multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) in all three Inclusive Learning Resource Centers (ILRCs) in Metro Manila.

The ILRCs are at Batino Elementary School in Quezon City, Alabang Elementary School in Muntinlupa City, and P. Gomez Elementary School in the City of Manila.

DepEd SPED Advisor Roland Montes initially described the ILRCs as operational, but Romulo responded, “How can it be operational when you don’t have an MDT?”

Play Video

An MDT, according to the law, facilitates assessments, monitoring, and evaluation of LWDs. The goal is to integrate these students into the basic education system through the guidance of professionals.

According to Section 8, “Each ILRC shall have an ILRC Supervisor and a multidisciplinary team.” The team shall be composed of any or all of the following:

Educational Psychologist

Guidance Counselor

Psychometrician

Developmental Pediatrician

Neurological Psychiatrist

Physical Therapist

Occupational Therapist

Speech and Language Therapist or Speech Correction Teacher

Speech Language Pathologist

Reading Specialist

Specialist for Braille and other augmentative and alternative modes of communication

FSL (Filipino Sign Language) Specialist

FSL Interpreter

Sign Communication or Visual Specialist

Special Needs Teacher

ILRC Supervisor

Romulo, the House basic education committee chairperson, said: “I just don’t want any parent to question us. That is why mayroong listahan. In fact, do’n sa mismong batas eh naglagay kami ng listahan (That is why there’s a list. In fact, we even included the list in the law itself).”

DepEd Assistant Secretary Jerome Buenviaje admitted that while the ILRCs are deemed operational, they have incomplete staff.

“According to our records, they’re partially operational, and MDTs are coming from partnerships from universities and other health agencies…. The MDTs aren’t complete yet, but we do have professionals in place,” he said in a mix of Filipino and English.

Romulo pointed out that certain professionals in MDTs, such as a developmental pediatrician, are essential in assessing each learner’s abilities and needs before they can be integrated into the education system.

“Ang inclusivity, kailangan may assessment. So kung walang assessment, dapat hindi natin [tatawaging] inclusivity kasi we don’t know how to handle [the students],” he said.

(Inclusivity requires assessment. So, without assessment, we shouldn’t call it inclusivity, because we don’t know how to handle the students.)

A study released by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) in November 2025 showed that most children with disabilities remain out of school.

“In SY 2024-2025, only 391,089 learners with disabilities were enrolled in public schools, representing just 8% of the estimated 5.1 million children with disabilities nationwide. The vast majority of children with disabilities remain either out-of-school or in-school but with an unidentified disability, indicating significant gaps in identification and enrollment,” states the study.

Not enough funds, materials

During the briefing, EDCOM 2 Executive Director Karol Mark Yee also pointed out that while the Special Needs Education Program budget increased to P1.04 billion in 2026, the funds are “unevenly distributed” among schools, “insufficient,” and “usually delayed.”

The funds are meant to cover learner assessments, additional teacher training, and inclusive learning materials, among others.

Given the budget, the DepEd estimates that there should be an average allocation of P1,400 per LWD for the school year. But EDCOM 2 findings show that some schools received as little as P333 per learner.

There is also a shortage or lack of access to educational materials for LWDs in most schools.

The usual learning aids are supposed to be converted into various inclusive formats, such as braille, large print, audio, digital copies, augmentative and alternative communication, and Filipino sign language.

“Under the IRR (implementing rules and regulations), the DepEd is authorized to convert learning resources into accessible formats. It also requires publishers to provide digital copies so it can then be adapted to the needs of learners with special needs,” Yee said.

Romulo told the education department to get a clear picture of what is actually happening in schools.

“The issue really is walang feedback sa inyo eh (there’s no feedback). You are not aware that this is happening on the ground…. We have to be more proactive,” the lawmaker said. – Rappler.com

World.title: VP Duterte’s bank docs may reveal more than AMLC reports – de Lima
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte —File photo by Grig C. Montegrande | INQUIRER

MANILA, Philippines — The bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte, which the Senate impeachment court will subpoena, could reveal a broader and more detailed financial picture than the transaction summaries previously submitted by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), according to Rep. Leila de Lima, a member of the House prosecution panel.

De Lima said the panel would want the complete records because the reports presented during the House proceedings might not represent every relevant transaction involving Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manasas Carpio.

“What we want is to show all. Whether it is more, this is less than what was initially reported by AMLC through those suspicious [transactions],” De Lima said in an interview on “On Point with Pinky Webb” on Bilyonaryo News Channel Monday night.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate subpoena on Duterte finance docs a ‘victory’ for people

The AMLC material identified P6.7 billion in alleged covered and suspicious transactions beginning from Duterte’s entry into public office as Davao City vice mayor and continuing into her vice presidency.

The House prosecution sought the source documents from the banks so they could examine the individual deposits, withdrawals, and transfers behind the aggregate figures, de Lima said.

According to her, the bank records will allow the parties to determine whether the transaction totals reflected repeated transfers, legitimate earnings, or funds that cannot be satisfactorily explained.

The banks will need to directly confirm the records, although they themselves generated the reports submitted to the AMLC, de Lima said.

Article continues after this 

The prosecution also expects the records to clarify the couple’s combined financial position and the assets held jointly or separately.

READ: Senate needs VP financial docs to rule on unexplained wealth

Article continues after this 

De Lima said the records could ultimately show a higher amount, a lower amount, or additional details not contained in the initial summaries.

“So it could be more,” De Lima added. /atm

World.title: Alan Cayetano dissent can’t overturn VP records ruling – prosecution
World.content:
Senator-judge Alan Peter Cayetano during Day 5 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on July 14, 2026. Also in the photo is Senator-judge Pia Cayetano. —File photo by Niño Jesus Orbeta | INQUIRER

MANILA, Philippines — The reported objection of Senator-judge Alan Peter Cayetano to the impeachment court’s ruling to subpoena the financial records of Vice President Sara Duterte will not by itself overturn that decision, according to the House prosecutors.

In a press conference on Tuesday, Rep. Jose Manuel Tadeo “Chel” Diokno and Atty. Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr., counsel for the House Panel of Prosecutors, said Cayetano’s objections would be put on record but would not by itself overturn the ruling to grant subpoenas for specified financial and tax records involving the vice president.

“Under the rules of the Senate for impeachment, a senator-judge always has the right to file [an objection] if he doesn’t agree with the decision of the impeachment courts,” Diokno said in a mix of Filipino and English.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate needs VP financial docs to rule on unexplained wealth

He said the prosecution would study the senator-judge’s reasoning once an opinion had actually been submitted instead of responding to reports about a document it had not yet seen.

“We just want to see the different view of our mga senator-judges. We will also look into that once it has been filed,” he said.

Right to explain disagreement

Tolosa also acknowledged Cayetano’s right to explain his disagreement but distinguished a dissenting opinion from a successful challenge to the court’s ruling.

“He has the right to dissent, but it will not change the ruling, of course. The ruling will stand,” Tolosa said.

Article continues after this 

On Monday, the impeachment court granted the prosecution’s request for subpoenas covering specified peso-denominated bank records, Anti-Money Laundering Council documents, and Bureau of Internal Revenue records relevant to the second article of impeachment, which alleges unexplained wealth and discrepancies between Duterte’s declared assets and financial activity.

The ruling excluded foreign-currency deposits and denied requests involving two entities for which the court found insufficient links. It also limited the use of records predating Duterte’s vice presidential term to establishing a financial baseline relevant to the allegations during her present term.

Article continues after this 

Under the impeachment rules governing evidence, a ruling by the presiding officer becomes the court’s ruling unless a senator-judge asks for a formal vote. Tolosa said this was the procedure explained during Monday’s proceedings.

“He can rule unless someone objects, in which case it can be put to a vote,” Tolosa said.

READ: Senate subpoena on Duterte finance docs a ‘victory’ for people

The court directed the concerned banks, AMLC, and BIR to submit their records or appropriate returns to the clerk of court on July 30.

The AMLC documents will first undergo an in-camera review, while the issuance of the BIR subpoena does not automatically authorize disclosure of confidential tax records.

The subpoenas authorize only the acquisition and court review of specified documents. But they do not establish the truth of the allegations under Article II, nor do they make the records automatically admissible or prevent the defense from challenging their relevance, interpretation, and evidentiary weight. /atm

World.title: Batangas City holds ‘bokashi ball’ throwing for river restoration
World.content:
The Batangas City government led a “bokashi ball” throwing event at Calumpang Bridge as part of its efforts to rehabilitate the river and improve its water quality. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

LUCENA CITY – The Batangas City government led a “bokashi ball” throwing event at Calumpang Bridge as part of its efforts to rehabilitate the river and improve its water quality.

Held as part of the city’s 57th Foundation Day celebration, hurling “bokashi balls” aims to restore river quality, strengthen environmental protection measures, and encourage greater community participation in keeping local waterways clean, the City Public Information Office (PIO) said in a report on Tuesday.

“Bokashi balls”, also known as mud balls, originated in Japan, where they are widely used to revive polluted waterways.

Article continues after this 

READ: Bayanihan and corporate social impact

They contain beneficial microorganisms that help break down organic waste, reduce foul odors, and decompose sludge accumulated in contaminated bodies of water, the PIO said, citing City Environment Officer Oliver Gonzales. Bokashi balls can also help improve soil quality.

According to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), a single bokashi ball can help treat approximately one cubic meter of sludge-laden water. This form of biotechnology has been used across the country, such as in the Manila Bay watershed.

“Through programs such as this, the Batangas City government continues to promote a clean, safe, and greener environment for the benefit of both present and future generations,” the PIO said.

The Calumpang River has a catchment area of about 472 square kilometers. It forms the southeastern boundary of Batangas City’s urban center before emptying into Batangas Bay.

Local authorities said the river has faced increasing environmental pressure from rapid urbanization and agricultural runoff over the years, prompting the implementation of watershed protection measures and river cleanup initiatives./coa

World.title: Missing university worker found dead in Bohol; nephew arrested
World.content:
An administrative officer of the Bohol Island State University (BISU)-Candijay Campus in Bohol province, who had been missing for two days, was found dead on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Authorities are investigating the incident. —Contributed photo

TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — A 33-year-old administrative officer of the Bohol Island State University (BISU)-Candijay Campus who had been missing for two days was found dead on Tuesday, with police arresting his nephew in connection with the killing.

The victim was identified as Dexter “Dex” Timbal Hinayon, a resident of Barangay Can-olin, Candijay, Bohol. He served as director of the Cashier’s Office at BISU-Candijay Campus and was also the store manager of Kusina Nitibo Restaurant.

Major Joseph Lopena, acting chief of the Provincial Community Affairs and Development Unit and information officer of the Bohol Police Provincial Office, said the Candijay Police Station received an update from the victim’s sister, Eunice, at about 9:25 a.m. on Tuesday.

Article continues after this 

READ: Man shot dead while cradling grandchild in Bohol

According to Lopena, the victim’s cellphone was recovered by the family at the restaurant. Information obtained from conversations stored on the device helped investigators identify a suspect and trace the location where Hinayon’s body was found.

Police discovered the victim’s body inside a sack in a grassy area of Nasarok Hills in Purok 3, Barangay Can-olin.

Investigators said Hinayon was allegedly strangled at one location before his body was dumped at another site nearby. His mouth had been taped shut, his hands were bound, and his knees and chest were secured with adhesive tape.

Police identified the suspect as Jesse Requiz, 18, the victim’s nephew. Requiz’s father is Hinayon’s first cousin.

Article continues after this 

Initial investigation showed that the suspect had allegedly demanded P2,000 from the victim. Hinayon reportedly gave him P1,000, which investigators believe triggered the fatal attack.

Lopena said police went to the school where the suspect was at the time and invited him for questioning. During the investigation, Requiz allegedly confessed to the crime.

Article continues after this 

Authorities have to file a murder case against the suspect as the investigation continues to determine the full circumstances surrounding the killing.

Hinayon’s death sent shockwaves through the BISU-Candijay community, where he was affectionately known as “Mr. Smile” for his cheerful personality and active involvement in community activities.

In a statement, the Campus Student Organizations of BISU-Candijay paid tribute to Hinayon.

“His smile, compassion, and the lives he influenced will continue to live on in the hearts of those who had the privilege of knowing him.”

The student organizations also extended their sympathies to the victim’s family and loved ones.

World.title: Manibela to hold 2-day transport strike on July 22-23
World.content:
Mar Valbuena, chair of the group Manibela, holds a press conference in this undated photo at the group’s headquarters in Sta. Mesa, Manila. Manibela announced Tuesday, July 21, that the group will hold a two-day transport strike on July 22-23. Photo by Gillian Villanueva

MANILA, Philippines — Transport group Manibela will hold a two-day transport strike on July 22-23, 2026 to protest the series of oil price hikes and the continued suspension of fare increases for public utility vehicles, the group announced on Tuesday.

The strike comes after diesel and kerosene prices posted fresh double-digit increases amid the ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

READ: Diesel, kerosene post new double-digit price jumps

Article continues after this 

The Department of Energy (DOE) has once again imposed price adjustments on petroleum products, with fuel companies allowed to implement a maximum hike of P10.68 per liter for diesel, P3.65 per liter for gasoline, and P11.77 per liter for kerosene.

In an advisory, Manibela criticized DOE for merely explaining the increases instead of holding oil companies accountable and protecting consumers.

“Due to the continuous failure of DOE to protect the public interest and failure to implement fare increase, MANIBELA will conduct a 2-day transport strike on Wednesday and Thursday on July 22-23, 2026,” the group said.

In a message to the INQUIRER, Manibela Chairperson Mar Valbuena said that the group’s strike center will be setp up at the Petron station along Philippine Coconut Authority (Philcoa) in Quezon City at 7 a.m. on Thursday.

READ: Manibela starts 3-day strike, hits gov’t ‘band-aid solutions’

Article continues after this 

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin earlier said the government would ensure there would be no hoarding or overpricing of fuel products, but acknowledged that global oil prices remain beyond the country’s control.

Meanwhile, the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) had approved fare increases for jeepneys, buses, airport taxis and transport network vehicle services in March, but President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. suspended their implementation before they took effect.

Article continues after this 

The INQUIRER sought the comment of Garin regarding Manibela’s statements. It has yet to receive a response as of this writing. /dp

World.title: La Union fisherman nabbed for fishing without a license
World.content:
Maritime law enforcers on Monday, July 20, 2026, arrested a 45-year-old La Union fisherman for setting off to fish in municipal waters without a license. INQUIRER FILES

CALASIAO, Pangasinan – Maritime law enforcers on Monday arrested a 45-year-old La Union fisherman for setting off to fish in municipal waters without a license.

A police report said the fisherman was apprehended off the waters of Sto. Tomas town by personnel of the Sto. Tomas Municipal Police Station and the Damortis Maritime Law Enforcement Team (MLET), during a seaborne patrol.

READ: 2 arrested for illegal fishing in Oriental Mindoro marine sanctuary

Article continues after this 

The man is facing charges for allegedly violating Chapter XV, Section 72 of Municipal Fishery Ordinance No. 2, Series of 2003, which prohibits unlicensed fishing within Sto. Tomas jurisdiction.

Authorities confiscated from the fisherman a motorized banca named “Heart of Mary” valued at P55,000, a set of fishing nets worth P10,000, and about two kilograms of assorted fish estimated at P350.

The suspect and the seized items were brought to the Damortis MLET Office for proper documentation and disposition./coa

World.title: House prosecutors deny VP Duterte impeached before evidence found
World.content:
Lawyer Benjamin Tolosa Jr. and Rep. Chel Diokno gives a press conference on the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. —Screenshot

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution, through Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” Diokno and lawyer Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr., denied the claim that Vice President Sara Duterte was impeached before any evidence was collected.

In a press conference, Diokno and Tolosa stressed that the House had already gathered sufficient evidence to approve the articles of impeachment, pointing out that the Senate impeachment trial would be the proper constitutional forum for the full presentation, examination, and testing of that evidence.

They were responding to a Facebook post made by Davao City Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte questioning why the prosecution sought Senate subpoenas for the bank and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records of Vice President Sara Z. Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, after the articles of impeachment had already been transmitted.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate subpoena on Duterte finance docs a ‘victory’ for people

Proper context

In his post written in Bisaya, Paolo Duterte reportedly portrayed the sequence as impeachment followed only afterward by a search for supporting documents.

According to Diokno, that remark confused the House committee on justice’s probable-cause inquiry with the full trial conducted by the impeachment court.

“We know, and we talked about that issue yesterday, that they were calling it a fishing expedition. But let’s put what we’re talking about in the proper context,” Diokno said in Filipino

Citing the Constitution, the prosecutors explained that the House initiates impeachment cases and determines whether the allegations should proceed to trial. Then it will be the Senate that will try and decide on the articles of impeachment, with the prosecution and defense presenting their evidence before the senator-judges.

Article continues after this 

“When the impeachment complaint reaches the committee on justice of the House of Representatives, the duty of the committee then was to determine if there was probable cause,” Diokno said.

“It’s not our job to dig up all the evidence and have a trial right away because it’s the Senate’s part to conduct a trial,” he went on.

Article continues after this 

“As you will notice, only a portion of the evidence was what the committee on justice saw,” he added.

Still, he pointed out, the House proceedings included documentary submissions and testimony used to determine probable cause, and the subpoena for evidence was made when the case reached the Senate impeachment court.

READ: Senate needs VP financial docs to rule on unexplained wealth

Subpoena request granted

On Monday, the impeachment court granted the prosecution’s requests for subpoenas covering specified peso-denominated bank records, Anti-Money Laundering Council documents, and the Bureau of Internal Revenue records of the vice president and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

The court did not, however, authorize an unrestricted examination. It excluded foreign-currency deposits and two corporations for which it found insufficient links.

The AMLC records will first undergo an in-camera review, while the BIR commissioner must make the appropriate return before the court determines what tax records may lawfully be produced.

Diokno said the sequence followed by the prosecution conformed to the Constitution rather than bypassing it.

“The process we followed was no different from that laid down in our Constitution. That’s why we believe, and we have repeatedly said, that there was no fishing expedition, no shortcut,” he said.

Like a criminal case

For his part, Tolosa compared the two-stage impeachment process to that followed in a criminal case, where prosecutors first determine probable cause before a full court trial.

He stressed that the comparison concerned the sequence of proceedings, not the evidentiary standard ultimately applicable to impeachment.

“As Cong. Chel said, before the House of Representatives, it’s determination of probable cause first. It’s the same in a criminal case before the prosecutor’s office — determination of probable cause first,” Tolosa said.

“It’s still not required and not expected for all the evidence to be presented. All the evidence will comte out during the trial itself,” he added.

According to the prosecutors, the subpoena ruling does not establish the truth of the allegations or make the requested records automatically admissible. The documents will still have to be produced, authenticated, and formally offered, and the defense may still object to their admission and explain the transactions recorded in them.
